[1083] The UN's special position

[1084] The United Nations (UN) has a special role in safeguarding the rules-based international order and is intended to contribute to ensuring that states' behavior is based on respect for international law, as well as maintaining international peace and security, equality between states and human rights

[1085] To safeguard Norwegian interests, it is crucial for the government that the system of international law institutions and rules function and are respected

[1086] Respect for international law is crucial for promoting an international legal order in which the use of force is regulated and regular

[1087] The UN Security Council has a special position in international law with the authority to make decisions that are binding under international law

[1088] In periods of heightened international tension, the Council's ability to handle global and regional challenges is hampered by internal disagreements among the Council's permanent members, which has meant that the Security Council has been paralyzed after Russia's attack on Ukraine

[1089] The implementation of the UN Sustainable Development Goals in the defense sector

[1090] The defense sector has the ambition to fulfill its tasks in line with the UN's Sustainable Development Goals

[1091] The sector influences social, business ethics, and climate and environmental conditions both directly, through its activities and employees, and by being a major purchaser and player with influence on others

[1092] The Sustainable Development Goals on peace, justice and security strike at the core of the sector's societal goals and encompass the work of maintaining a security political order through an international state of peace, a state of justice, a state of security, as well as the need to adapt the sector to a changing climate

[1093] The ability to maintain a security policy order over time is an expression of sustainability

[1094] The strategic and knowledge-based work on values, leadership, culture, equality and diversity in the defense sector will be strengthened as part of the work on social sustainability

[1095] This will be necessary to safeguard defense capabilities and our own personnel, but also to maintain trust and a willingness to defend in the general population

[1096] The defense sector should more clearly operationalize and communicate internally and externally the values ​​it strives for

[1097] The value work should be integrated into processes, tools and training, and should contribute to developing professional leaders who are good role models who internalize the sector's values ​​and systematically build and maintain a value-based culture

[1098] This includes integrating a gender and equality perspective throughout the sector

[1099] Climate change and loss of nature constitute one of the greatest challenges of our time

[1100] The defense sector shall work systematically and holistically to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, minimize environmental impact, and safeguard natural and cultural values ​​associated with the sector's overall activities

[1101] The sector is working to reduce energy consumption and increase local renewable energy production

[1102] Through cooperation in the sector, efforts will be made to adapt infrastructure, property, buildings, facilities, equipment, exercises, operations and preparedness in line with climate change

[1103] Procurement in the defense sector can help support the defense sector in reducing negative climate and environmental impacts, and promoting climate and environmentally friendly solutions and reuse

[1104] Russia and China are increasingly adopting different interpretations of international law than Western countries in key areas

[1105] Furthermore, the significant changes in global power relations could contribute to further weakening both the legitimacy and effectiveness of the Security Council

[1106] In the UN context, the government will place great emphasis on a holistic approach to safeguarding our foreign and security policy interests, and not least directing efforts towards areas where we have national interests – but also towards fields where Norway has expertise and experience

[1107] The Government will, among other things, continue its efforts to ensure that the Security Council pays greater attention to how climate change affects international peace and security

[1108] UN peacekeeping operations help prevent, limit and stop conflicts

[1109] The Government will contribute to ensuring that UN peacekeeping operations remain a key instrument for international peace and security

[1110] Norway has both a responsibility and a vested interest in contributing to these peace operations with its own forces and personnel

[1111] Therefore, the Armed Forces will continue to contribute highly qualified personnel, emphasize women's participation and nominate candidates for leadership positions, which could lead to more effective peace operations and continue the strong support for the UN Secretariat's reform work

[1112] Furthermore, the government wants to be an active contributor to the UN reform process to make UN peace operations more modern and relevant, including in connection with the reform efforts of the UN Secretary-General and the initiative to mobilize resources for UN peace operations

[1115] In this context, emphasis is placed on contributions that strengthen personnel safety and the protection of civilians

[1116] Implications for Norwegian security

[1117] Intensified great power rivalry

[1118] Russia's attack on Ukraine has reinforced and actualized a security policy development that was announced over several years

[1119] The increased rivalry between China and the United States, between authoritarian and democratic states, and new constellations of partners and supporters globally and regionally mean that the government's work for peace, security, values, and a world order based on international law is inextricably linked to stronger and more integrated Western cooperation

[1120] Rivalry over worldviews and values is becoming more prominent and is threatening the international legal order where justice takes precedence over might

[1121] The relationship between NATO and Russia is characterized by confrontation and intervenes in all domains and geographical areas where Russian and allied interests meet

[1122] The war in Ukraine reinforces Russia's needs and ambitions for strategic dominance in the Arctic and the ability for global power projection

[1123] Russia uses extensive, ruthless and international law-violating military force to achieve its goals

[1124] The outcome of the war in Ukraine is far from decided

[1125] The situation is unclear and can change quickly

[1126] The government is prepared for the conflict to be protracted and for the human suffering and material costs to be enormous

[1127] This will require long-term thinking and flexibility in Norway's political, civilian and military support

[1128] Over time, Russia has increasingly challenged the international legal order

[1129] This is a development that will most likely continue, also based on closer Russian cooperation with China

[1130] The challenge from China is growing, and China has not distanced itself from Russia's war of aggression

[1131] Instability and risk of conflict Norway and our allies are in a situation characterized by increased unpredictability, uncertainty and instability that is likely to persist

[1132] In addition, we are faced with an increased ability and willingness to use military force to achieve political goals

[1133] The war in Ukraine, the situation in the Middle East and increased tension in Asia are examples of how the security situation can change radically in a short time, and how the long-term perspective is characterized by instability and uncertainty

[1134] Significantly greater geopolitical unpredictability entails an increased risk of military conflict affecting Norway or allies, through escalation, or through a conflict spreading to nearby Norwegian areas

[1135] A security policy climate characterized by mutual distrust and reduced contact surfaces increases the risk of misunderstandings, the need for marking, and unintentional escalation dynamics

[1136] This also increases the risk of strategic misunderstandings

[1137] Russian military power remains the defining challenge to Norwegian and allied security in Europe

[1138] Russia appears as an unstable and unpredictable actor with few signs of a change in political course

[1139] Uncertainty about Russian intentions and certainty about Russia's willingness to use force to achieve its strategic goals have increased

[1140] This means that Norway must be better prepared for a more dangerous and unpredictable Russia

[1141] Norwegian authorities must assume that allies, as part of deterrence against Russia, will be more present in Norwegian areas, especially in the north

[1142] Security policy room for manoeuvre Norway's security policy room for manoeuvre is under pressure

[1143] A main challenge for Norwegian security is the increased risk of being marginalized, meaning that our interests or security are not taken into account

[1144] As the potential for conflict in our areas has increased, our ability to understand, shape, coordinate, and participate in activity in our areas becomes more important

[1145] In this way, Norwegian authorities can prevent escalation to levels where our national freedom of action and influence are significantly reduced

[1146] Security challenges will challenge national security in several areas at any time, not just in times of crisis and war

[1147] Change can and will happen quickly, often dictated by a few dominant actors

[1148] This includes strategies of competition and confrontation below the threshold of direct armed conflict

[1149] Norwegian authorities can quickly find themselves in undesirable choice situations that restrict Norwegian freedom of action and ability to pursue and promote Norwegian security interests

[1150] The security situation is also characterized by the transition between peace, crisis and war becoming less clear and more dynamic

[1151] In addition, rapid technological development gives Norway a number of advantages, but also increased vulnerability

[1152] New and groundbreaking technology can reinforce this development

[1153] The Armed Forces must deal with expanded and complex areas of operation that are constantly changing

[1154] Climate change will open up larger areas of operation and create new challenges and opportunities for Norway, our allies, and Russia

[1155] The connection between the security situation in the Baltic Sea region and the High North means that all of Norway and surrounding sea areas are one area of interest and operation, which in turn is part of a larger community of interests and allied area of operation in Europe and the North Atlantic

[1156] Security challenges will also affect national security in digital and outer space

[1157] The increased strategic importance of the High North has consequences for Norway's security policy space for action, and reinforces the need and likelihood of military signaling and demonstrations of force in our immediate vicinity from both the Russian and allied sides

[1158] Climate change and Europe's dependence on stable energy supplies are also drawing military attention to the High North

[1159] Overall, the development is challenging the ability of Norwegian authorities to set the stage, influence, shape activity and exert influence

[1160] For Norway, it is of great importance that the Armed Forces can exert influence on the security situation by shaping, coordinating and participating in the increased allied activity that is taking place in our immediate areas

[1161] The conflict spectrum The conflict spectrum describes generic types of situations in our military-strategic environment that can occur simultaneously to varying degrees in peace, crisis and war

[1162] Competition is a low-intensity normal state

[1163] Here, the room for action of Norway, its allies and threat actors is continuously exposed to “soft” influence and pressure from the environment

[1164] The dynamics and interaction between the players will affect the individual player's position in the competition

[1165] Confrontation can quickly vary in intensity and occurs increasingly in daily life

[1166] Norwegian and allied security is exposed to direct or indirect influence, pressure and threats that require clear handling

[1167] The situation can be confusing and perceived as demanding

[1168] Conflict is a high-intensity, very serious and unstable situation

[1169] Norway and its allies are exposed to direct and harmful influence, attacks and threats that include the threat or use of extensive destructive force

[1170] consolidation is situations where actors seek to consolidate advantageous positions achieved in competition, confrontation or conflict

[1171] NATO expansion links Norway and our surrounding areas more directly to the Baltic Sea region due to the strategic location of the North Sea

[1172] This reinforces the importance of the High North as one of Russia's most important areas of operation

[1173] Norwegian and allied freedom of action to operate on and from Norwegian territory and territorial waters is becoming more important, especially in light of a united Nordic region in NATO

[1174] This also increases the importance of Norway's maritime capacity in the north

[1175] Strengthened allied cohesion

[1176] In a deteriorating security situation, allied unity and NATO cooperation are strengthened and absolutely crucial

[1177] Among allies, there is broad recognition of the need to strengthen the alliance and the collective defense capabilities of member states

[1178] This means that Norwegian authorities can expect more from allies, but also that NATO and allies expect more from Norway

[1179] Both in terms of how we strengthen our national defense capabilities, and in terms of our contributions to joint allied efforts

[1180] The government's main line is to contribute to a common approach among allies and like-minded countries in dealing with Russia

[1181] At the same time, Norwegian policy regarding Russia must continue to be recognizable

[1182] Being recognizable and predictable does not necessarily mean doing exactly the same thing as before, when the situation has changed

[1183] The strategic challenge is therefore how the Armed Forces, together with allies and with the civilian actors in the total defense, will solve its tasks in a security situation characterized by rivalry, unpredictability, instability and the risk of escalation in order to defend Norwegian security and maintain Norwegian room for maneuver

[1184] The starting point for this long-term plan

[1185] Implementation of previous plans

[1186] In 2021, the government took over the implementation of a long-term plan that was ambitious and that moved in the right direction in several areas

[1187] Implementation of the measures from this and previous long-term plans, with the phasing in of new materiel systems, the establishment of new departments and the implementation of necessary updates, will gradually increase the Armed Forces' operational capability

[1188] Several important milestones for the development of the Armed Forces have been achieved

[1189] F-35 fighter jets have taken over NATO's combat readiness and P-8 maritime patrol aircraft have replaced the P-3C Orion

[1190] The Coast Guard has been supplied with new helicopter-carrying vessels to replace the Nordkapp class, and a contract has been signed for the acquisition of new submarines

[1191] The modernization of the Army is ongoing with the phasing in of new artillery, the phasing in of combat air defense, more combat vehicles and new tanks

[1192] The establishment of Finnmark Land Defense has come a long way and has increased the permanent land military presence in Finnmark

[1193] The government has also strengthened the Home Guard beyond the planned ambition

[1194] However, in several areas there are challenges in achieving set goals

[1195] As the government explained in Report

[1196] St. 10 (2021–2022) found significant weaknesses in several key assumptions in the previous long-term plan

[1197] Too few resources were planned for property, buildings and facilities, and insufficient funds were set aside for maintenance

[1198] The equipment and ammunition stocks were planned at too low a level to sustain continued increased activity

[1199] With this starting point, and with the deterioration in the security situation, immediate and targeted investment in the Armed Forces was necessary

[1200] The government has implemented this with several specific measures that were important to prioritize, based on assessments and advice from the Chief of Defence

[1201] It was crucial for the government that the measures implemented in the short term also build on the development of the Armed Forces in a longer perspective

[1202] In addition to several temporary reinforcements, the government has increased allocations to the defense sector through the annual budgets to a level that is NOK 11.4 billion above what was expected

[1203] This includes support for Ukraine through the defense budget

[1204] The priorities have been aimed at strengthening supply readiness, increased maintenance of the building stock, facilitating increased allied presence, strengthening the Home Guard and the Intelligence Service and increasing education quotas, as well as strengthening staffing in the Armed Forces

[1205] The implementation of the previous long-term plan is behind schedule

[1206] Measures to recruit, train and retain personnel have not been sufficient

[1207] The effort to modernize the sector's ICT solutions is significantly behind schedule

[1208] There are challenges related to lack of implementation capacity and delayed realization of benefits in the improvement work

[1209] The defense sector has not succeeded in releasing economic gains in line with the target of NOK 2.3 billion

[1210] The war in Ukraine has contributed to the implementation of measures from previous and earlier plans in some areas taking somewhat longer than expected

[1211] Through the consideration of Prop

[1212] S (2021–2022) the Storting allocated 3 billion kroner to meet developments in the security policy situation with concrete measures to increase preparedness and presence in our local areas

[1213] This initiative has had positive effects

[1214] Support for Ukraine's defensive war is important, also for Norway's security

[1215] The Armed Forces' assistance has been significant and has had several positive effects

[1216] The efforts in connection with donations of equipment and training of Ukrainian soldiers have also reduced our own operational capability in certain areas, and tied up resources in a pressured personnel and expertise situation

[1217] The government believes that this has been the right priority

[1218] The direction set out in previous plans has provided a good starting point for strengthening the Armed Forces

[1219] The Chief of Defence, through his expert military council, has agreed to the structure of the previous plans

[1220] The same applies to the Defence Commission

[1221] Therefore, in this long-term plan, the government will build on the development direction that the previous long-term plan was based on

[1222] Significant weaknesses have been identified within the current organization and structure, which must be improved if strengthening the defense capability is to be successful

[1223] In the government's view, rectification of these weaknesses must be prioritized, in order to better facilitate the structure the Armed Forces have today, and future structures that have already been adopted in the previous and earlier plans, achieving the expected operational capability

[1224] The Armed Forces' operational capability and preparedness

[1225] The Armed Forces have increased both operational activity and presence in priority areas in recent years

[1226] This has resulted in a greater strain on the structure as a whole

[1227] A high pace of operations over time has in some areas led to personnel attrition, as well as a greater need for maintenance of equipment

[1228] Combined with somewhat reduced availability due to aging materiel and a generational change within several materiel systems, this at times challenges the Armed Forces' ability to carry out the planned activity

[1229] Overall, however, the ability to conduct daily national operations has so far been satisfactory

[1230] The Armed Forces have maintained a presence in prioritized areas and contributed to establishing a good situational understanding

[1231] Increased allied presence in our immediate areas has contributed positively and compensated for varying availability of Norwegian capacities, especially at sea

[1232] Good coordination of allied presence is important to safeguard Norwegian interests

[1233] The Armed Forces have implemented heightened vigilance and preparedness in line with national and allied planning

[1234] As part of this, targeted prioritization of the Armed Forces' operational efforts to protect Norwegian energy production was carried out, in close collaboration with allies and civilian actors

[1235] Operational consequences for Norwegian defense capabilities of Norwegian support to Ukraine

[1236] Effective military support to Ukraine helps safeguard Norwegian security interests

[1237] The need for support may persist over time, even if the fighting ends

[1238] Norway's support to Ukraine is provided within the framework of the Nansen Programme, adopted by the Storting on 16 February

[1239] The military part of the support consists mainly of donations of equipment from the defense sector, procurement through multinational cooperation and mechanisms, procurement directly from industry, as well as training and education

[1240] Efforts are being made to provide military support to Ukraine in cooperation with allies and partners, both because of the effect it can have for Ukraine, but also because it can provide useful learning and cooperation that can strengthen the defense of Norway

[1241] The agencies in the defense sector contribute with, among other things, training and education of Ukrainian personnel both in Norway and abroad, preparation and transport of equipment for donation, and replacement of equipment that has been donated

[1242] The need for such support will likely persist

[1243] All parts of the defense sector will be tasked with contributing to military support – and at the same time solving their primary missions nationally and within an alliance framework

[1244] The operational consequences of the resource allocation will be limited, but may come at the expense of other tasks that the defense sector must perform

[1245] For example, there have been cases where maintenance tasks have been reprioritized in favor of preparing equipment donated to Ukraine

[1246] The consequences of such reprioritizations may materialize over time

[1247] It cannot therefore be ruled out that military support to Ukraine will have unforeseen consequences for the Armed Forces' operational capability

[1248] At the same time, the operational value of the experience gained by personnel contributing as instructors for Ukrainian forces, or of knowledge transfer from Ukrainian personnel with combat experience, should not be underestimated

[1249] A significant part of the military support to Ukraine in 2022 and 2023 consisted of donations of military equipment that is in use in the defense sector

[1250] In the short term, the negative consequences of such donations may be that the structure becomes smaller than NATO's capability goals indicate, or that the Armed Forces' operational capability and our national preparedness are reduced for a period until the donated equipment is replaced

[1251] There is also a risk that less material than necessary is available for competence production, practice and training

[1252] When military equipment donated to Ukraine is to be reacquired, the procurement is carried out in the same demanding market for defense equipment as all other investments

[1253] What is being reacquired is generally more modern equipment

[1254] Scarcity of input factors, combined with high demand, is making lead times increasingly long

[1255] There is therefore a risk that the time from the time a donation is made until the equipment is reacquired will be longer than expected

[1256] This may lead to a temporary reduction in the Armed Forces' operational capability and delays in the planned development of the Armed Forces' structure

[1257] A gradually increased focus on the Armed Forces in recent years has resulted in improved responsiveness and an improved ability to conduct national operations

[1258] Increased cooperation with allies, international contributions and participation in multinational exercises have also contributed positively

[1259] Overall, important steps have therefore been taken in the right direction to increase operational capability

[1260] There are still significant challenges and operational weaknesses that require prioritization and further targeted efforts, including those related to personnel, material readiness, ammunition, ICT and property, buildings and structures

[1261] The structure is not robust enough, and does not have what it takes to be able to solve assigned tasks in a war situation

[1262] The defence's endurance is limited due to inadequate emergency stocks of ammunition for combat platforms, spare parts, and other supply classes

[1263] The challenges are exacerbated by a marginally staffed structure and aging equipment in several areas

[1264] The Defence Commission points out that the Chief of Defence's assessments of operational capability (VOE) must be based to a greater extent on realistic assessments of defence capability, and that the purpose and method must be clarified

[1265] The Government supports the recommendation, and will facilitate the presentation of the status of the Armed Forces to the Storting in a more appropriate manner

[1266] In addition to highly classified information presented in a closed format, the Storting and the public will, as previously, be informed in writing about the status at a general and unclassified level through text in the annual budget proposal

[1267] Critical gaps and deficiencies

[1268] Personnel and expertise

[1269] The Government has implemented and planned a number of measures to strengthen the Armed Forces' responsiveness and endurance, including increased staffing in selected areas

[1270] The government's ambitions for personnel growth are reflected in the defense budgets and in measures to increase educational capacity, measures to recruit and retain employees, and strengthening personnel-related property, buildings and facilities

[1271] The measures have improved the personnel situation in the desired direction, and by the end of 2024, the Armed Forces will be ahead of the already adopted personnel escalation

[1272] Small and vulnerable expertise environments and marginal access to systems expertise within several areas also entail a risk of not achieving agreed ambitions

[1273] This is reinforced by a pressured situation related to property, buildings and structures, particularly for residential, educational and work purposes

[1274] It takes time to increase the number of candidates at the Armed Forces' educational institutions, and the time it takes for new graduates to build practical experience is long

[1275] Sufficient access to people with the right expertise will therefore be a bottleneck for strengthening the Armed Forces, both in the short and long term

[1276] More measures in this area should have been outlined and planned in previous long-term plans, and this plan must address the consequences of this not having been given sufficient priority previously

[1277] The skills gaps the sector is experiencing today and expects in the years ahead are a result of both internal and external developments that stretch back several decades

[1278] The Norwegian Armed Forces have undergone extensive change and restructuring, in which the number of people on active duty has been halved from just over 50,000 in 1990 to just over 25,000 today

[1279] In addition, the Armed Forces' structure was changed from managing a mobilizable war structure of approximately 320,000 people to delivering requested capacities for international efforts

[1280] In sum, this has resulted in a need for fewer officers at mid- and higher-level and more specialists and commanders with more experience at lower levels

[1281] Both the structure and capacity of the Armed Forces' education system have been adapted to these new needs

[1282] Although the Armed Forces have strengthened the operational part of their operations over time, the Armed Forces still have an overly extensive staff structure

[1283] One challenge with this is that personnel quickly advance away from operational departments as the organization has a disproportionate number of positions at higher levels compared to the lower levels

[1284] This situation exacerbates the challenges associated with adequately staffing parts of the organization

[1285] The current personnel situation is also characterized by the fact that the extent of accidental departures is increasing more than expected in some areas, an ongoing aging wave with many employees retiring, and low unemployment is giving the defense sector strong competition for expertise and labor

[1286] Altogether, this means that the sector is in a demanding situation, where circumstances negatively affect both the departure and access to personnel and expertise

[1287] The government's measures to strengthen the personnel and competence area are presented in Chapter

[1288] Materiel and ammunition stocks

[1289] The defense sector's stockpiles of critical supplies such as materiel, fuel, and ammunition are too low and must be strengthened to achieve improved sustainment

[1290] In the event of a conflict situation in our immediate areas, Norway will be dependent on allied reinforcements

[1291] In an initial phase, before the Allied reinforcements have established their own supply lines, Norway must contribute critical supplies such as fuel for air forces

[1292] Norway's supply readiness is therefore necessary to contribute to the readiness and endurance of its own and allied forces, especially in the initial phase of a conflict

[1293] There are major challenges related to availability and lead time for certain types of ammunition, and it is necessary to stop inventory erosion

[1294] The need to procure critical supplies to achieve satisfactory inventory levels is a high priority

[1295] See more about the government's plan for increased supply readiness in chapters 3, 4, 5 and

[1296] Defence sector property, buildings and structures

[1297] The Armed Forces must have sufficient and functional buildings and infrastructure to be able to safeguard and protect materiel and equipment, support operational capability and accommodate personnel

[1298] Property, buildings and structures have not been sufficiently taken into account in the development of the Armed Forces

[1299] Not enough building stock has been planned and not enough funds have been allocated for maintenance

[1300] The Armed Forces have a lot of old buildings that are not adapted to today's requirements for living standards, workplaces and equipment

[1301] Over time, this has led to a significant maintenance backlog, with a great need for renewal and more capacity in the form of, among other things, barracks, housing, teaching facilities, training facilities and workshops

[1302] Insufficient capacity for appropriate and adapted property and infrastructure weakens the defense sector's operational capability

[1303] The development of bilateral and collective planning has increased the needs for buildings and infrastructure related to allied reception, exercises and training

[1304] Barracks and housing are important for recruiting and retaining personnel throughout the country

[1305] Today, there is a major shortage of barracks and housing, and much of what exists is in great need of maintenance

[1306] Housing and dormitories for defense personnel and barracks for conscripts in their first year of service have not been given sufficient priority

[1307] In addition, the building capacity at educational institutions must be increased to be able to handle an increased educational need

[1308] It is therefore important to increase capacity quickly, in addition to maintaining or upgrading the quality of existing facilities, so that the buildings have an increased lifespan

[1309] Property, buildings and structures have been given low priority over time, and it has been assumed that existing buildings and infrastructure will be reused when investing in new weapons systems and personnel escalation

[1310] Large bases such as Evenes, Setermoen and Terningmoen have expanded their activities, without corresponding growth in building stock and infrastructure

[1311] The condition of the defense sector's property stock has had a negative development, and parts of the property portfolio have a condition level that is too low

[1312] A deterioration in the condition level can, in the short term, lead to unintended shutdowns in operations and restrictions on use, or closure of buildings for health reasons

[1313] Poor condition increases the need for maintenance

[1314] The management model for property in the defense sector means that the Ministry of Defense owns the sector's property, Forsvarsbygg is the manager, and the Defense and other agencies are users

[1315] Today's rental model is based on Defence Building invoicing the Armed Forces and other users of buildings and other property

[1316] The rent does not cover the costs of renewal, replacement and maintenance, and is thus not sustainable

[1317] Today, Forsvarsbygg has an important role as an advisor to the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces and other users

[1318] This advisory function does not function optimally today in either needs assessment, investment projects or ongoing management

[1319] The current financing model does not cover the real costs of management, operation and maintenance

[1320] It will not be possible to catch up with the current large maintenance backlog without changes to the current model

[1321] Further investment in the defense sector's property, buildings and facilities is described in Chapter

[1322] Information and communication technology (ICT

[1323] Today's defense systems are digital, and effective utilization requires robust communication solutions and large data capacity

[1324] This also means that the defense sector must have the expertise to use and exploit the opportunities offered by modern ICT

[1325] Through the two previous long-term plans, a significant renewal of ICT in the defense sector has been planned

[1326] Realization of the initiative is significantly behind the expected plan

[1327] This negatively affects the Armed Forces' operational capability, and further strengthening and development of the Armed Forces will have a reduced effect if the necessary ICT is not put in place

[1328] Accessible and robust ICT services are necessary for the Armed Forces to carry out their most important tasks, and are a prerequisite for the ability to establish situational awareness, lead military forces and achieve the full effect of new capabilities

[1329] Modern ICT solutions are important for collaborating with allies and with actors in total defense

[1330] It is also crucial for the efficient operation of business in the defense sector

[1331] Fully or partially outdated ICT systems therefore pose a significant risk to defense capabilities

[1332] The government's focus on ICT and digitalization is presented in Chapter

[1333] Economic basis for new long-term plan

[1334] The annual appropriations from the Storting have largely been in line with the economic escalation path that the Storting agreed to when considering Bill No

[1335] The previous long-term plan was based on a significant financial boost, with particular emphasis on investments in new equipment, as well as increased staffing and a continuation of the level of training and exercises

[1336] At the same time, several risk elements were pointed out that could affect the defense economy and the economic scope for action

[1337] Examples include a more currency-exposed defense budget, and faster technological development requiring more continuous modernization of the Armed Forces' structure and capabilities

[1338] The most important uncertainty was related to developments in the security situation, and the security situation's significance for readiness requirements and the defense economy

[1339] Several of the aforementioned conditions have affected implementation and thereby challenged the economic room for maneuver in the sector

[1340] It must be expected that many of the same risk elements will also be present in this long-term plan

[1341] A seriously deteriorating security situation forms a bleak backdrop for the priorities set in this long-term plan

[1342] A significant economic boost is necessary to safeguard national and allied security, defense, and preparedness

[1343] Further financial escalation for the realization of this plan is described

[1344] in Chapter 6. Part II

[1345] Security and defense policy frameworks and guidelines

[1346] The organization of Norway's defense capabilities

[1347] Strategic orientation

[1348] Maintaining Norway's security will be more demanding in the future

[1349] Our ability to prevent, avert and manage a crisis or war must be significantly strengthened

[1350] The seriousness emphasizes the importance of increased national capacity for continuous presence and efforts to contribute to stability in our surrounding areas

[1351] This long-term plan assumes that Norway must take greater responsibility for its own and allied security, nationally and internationally, and contribute to stability and predictability in our immediate areas

[1352] Norwegian authorities must at all times be able to protect and safeguard influence and freedom of action, and continuously pursue and promote our strategic interests

[1353] The ability to make independent decisions and to be able to resist pressure, handle episodes and incidents, stand firm in crises, avoid attacks and prevent war is central to the further development of security and defense policy

[1354] There is therefore a need for a clearer strategic orientation for the development and application of the Armed Forces

[1355] Such an arrangement builds on Norway's core interests and on the continuity of Norwegian security and defense policy

[1356] The Government bases the strategic orientation of the Armed Forces on the fact that Norway must primarily focus its defense efforts on preventing conflict, in continuous and close cooperation with allies

[1357] Civil-military cooperation should support this

[1358] Furthermore, the Armed Forces must be more prepared for the possibility that conflict may nevertheless occur, and be able to respond in a timely manner and with relevant means of force, together with allies

[1359] Norwegian security must be defended every day, on and outside Norwegian territory

[1360] This is primarily to prevent and hinder others, directly or indirectly, from imposing their will on Norway by force, and if necessary by acting and responding with force if that happens

[1361] The Defence of Norway is increasingly about how the Defence Forces are organized to protect values, promote interests and contribute to collective deterrence and reassurance every day, in close and continuous cooperation with allies

[1362] This also includes the ability to respond quickly and effectively to challenges where and when they arise, and preparedness for rapid force buildup and the ability to defend the country together with allies in the event of armed conflict

[1363] Such a structure requires, firstly, an emphasis on strengthening the ability to exert influence and increased room for manoeuvre to safeguard stability in our immediate areas, and secondly, to prepare the Armed Forces for continuous use and efforts, at home and abroad, within an allied framework

[1364] The situation entails a need for more and more available forces with short reaction times, increased manning, the ability to be present in priority areas in a timely manner, and to cooperate with allied forces

[1365] Strengthening national capabilities must also be geared towards supporting close and integrated allied cooperation across the entire spectrum of conflicts, not least to support NATO as an effective guarantor of Norwegian and allied security

[1366] Norway's sovereignty and territorial integrity are defended together with others

[1367] As a political and military alliance, NATO and the Collective Security Treaty Organization have formed the framework for Norwegian security, with mutual obligations that ensure the freedom and independence of people and society

[1368] The Government has therefore based its work on this long-term plan on the following strategic priorities

[1369] These priorities largely correspond to the Defense Commission's assessments and the Chief of Defense's main message in the Technical Military Council

[1370] To emphasize the ability to prevent and deter conflict in close cooperation with allies To further develop the Armed Forces for increased national influence and room for action To organize the Armed Forces for continuous efforts in cooperation with our allies To contribute with relevant combat power for the defense of Norwegian and allied security To support NATO as a credible and effective guarantor of allied security To adapt the Armed Forces to contribute to operational and technological relevance

[1371] Overall, the structure and these priorities form the framework for updating security and defense policy goals, the defense concept, and the Armed Forces' tasks and associated ambitions

[1372] This also includes updating how the various elements of the defense concept work together to reinforce each other

[1373] The security and defense policy objectives express what the government wants to achieve with security and defense policy, and in sum constitute the defense sector's societal goals

[1374] They are the goal of all defense efforts, and guide the defense sector's understanding of its mission

[1375] The goals should contribute to continuity and long-term development of the sector, and in subsequent management

[1376] The government has updated the security and defense policy goals based on the security situation and the strategic orientation

[1377] The goals continue the core of the security and defense policy goals from the previous long-term plan

[1378] At the same time, the design of the goals has been simplified and tightened

[1379] The goals clarify what Norway will defend, explain in general terms how this is defended, and provide guidance for the further development of the defense sector

[1380] Security and defense policy goals

[1381] The security and defense policy goals are

[1382] Norwegian security and defense policy aims to defend Norwegian sovereignty, territorial integrity, population, democratic governance and our freedom of action against political, military and other pressure by contributing to

[1383] – Prevent armed conflict and the emergence of threats to Norwegian and allied security – Defend Norway and allies against threats, attacks and attacks within an allied framework – Promote Norwegian security interests, including peace, stability and international legal order Norway shall primarily direct its defense efforts towards preventing and counteracting conflict

[1384] Norwegian influence and room for action is greatest in the lower part of the conflict spectrum

[1385] It is therefore crucial for Norway to contribute to preventing and deterring the use of force against Norwegian strategic interests

[1386] In this way, Norwegian authorities can prevent further escalation to levels where our national freedom of action and influence are significantly reduced

[1387] The risk of military conflict involving Norway or allies has increased

[1388] Through credible military capability and daily operations, Norwegian military efforts will help prevent and deter pressure, threats and attacks so that situations do not develop into conflict

[1389] If Norway nevertheless becomes involved in a conflict, the Armed Forces, as part of an integrated allied defense effort, shall continue to safeguard Norwegian interests and be able to contribute to defending Norway or allies against enemy attacks and threats

[1390] This includes the ability to conduct high-intensity joint operations both on its own and with allies at short notice

[1391] Norwegian security, prosperity and development require a well-regulated international system in which the legitimate interests of smaller states are respected and protected

[1392] Norway's value creation and utilization of our resources, including valuable natural resources, must be secured, and if necessary defended, against external pressure, influence and attack

[1393] Norway is an Arctic, Atlantic, Nordic and European state, which is integrated into the international system through trade, finance, technology development, competence development and climate change management

[1394] Norway is affected by unrest and instability elsewhere in the world, and has a shared responsibility to prevent conflicts and prevent them from spreading

[1395] Our regional and global orientation is a strength for Norway and Norwegian security, but also creates obligations beyond Norway's borders

[1396] The defense of Norway thus encompasses the breadth of national and allied security and the protection of our national security interests

[1397] Military power is a security policy instrument and one of several instruments a sovereign state has to protect its interests, safeguard national independence and political freedom of action, across the entire spectrum of conflicts

[1398] In this context, the Armed Forces are a crucial instrument for safeguarding Norwegian and allied security, protecting Norwegian interests and values, facilitating cooperation and integrated collaboration with allies, and making credible contributions to our collective security within the framework of NATO

[1399] The Defence Concept The Norwegian Defence Concept constitutes a comprehensive approach to defending Norwegian security, in line with the security and defence policy goals

[1400] The defense concept and our overall defense capability fundamentally consist of three interdependent main elements

[1401] The armed forces' own capabilities, the defense capability through allied and regional cooperation and collective deterrence and defense capability within the framework of NATO, and the support that can be mustered from civil society, also within the framework of total defense

[1402] A wide range of civilian total defense actors and mechanisms support both national and allied military forces operating in Norway and its surrounding areas

[1403] Alliance affiliation is crucial for the defense of Norway and Norwegian security interests

[1404] The allied dimension encompasses the security guarantee, the collective approach to deterrence and defence within NATO, as well as bilateral, regional and multinational frameworks for cooperation, collaboration and reinforcement

[1405] This is expressed in strategies, concepts, plans, agreements, operations, presence and mutual representation in staffs and commands

[1406] The defense concept describes how Norway's defense capability is made up of three interdependent components

[1407] Alliance cooperation, Total Defence and civil society, and the Armed Forces

[1408] The defense concept describes the connection between the security and defense policy goals and the tasks of the Armed Forces, with ambition and associated capabilities

[1409] The Norwegian Armed Forces shall be organized so that national and allied efforts provide simultaneous and mutually reinforcing effects for Norwegian security, across the entire spectrum of conflicts, supported by the Total Defence Force

[1410] The defense of Norway is maintained through continuous national efforts on and outside Norwegian territory in peace, crisis and war, and facilitating allied efforts in Norway and in our surrounding areas

[1411] This contributes to both deterrence and reassurance

[1412] The defence's own capabilities comprise the total resources the defence sector can muster within its own organisation

[1413] A strong national defense with a credible ability to utilize, facilitate, and interact with all elements of the concept in peace, crisis, and war is a fundamental prerequisite for building the necessary defense capability

[1414] The Armed Forces should be able to provide Norway with a set of action options within the framework of allied and international cooperation and collaboration

[1415] As a security policy instrument, the Armed Forces' most important contribution to our security is therefore to exercise Norwegian influence and provide increased security policy room for action, in peace, crisis and war

[1416] In the face of combinations of military and non-military use of force, the Armed Forces contribute to the defense of Norway through continuous operations, integrated with others, and by being present in prioritized geographical areas to help ensure that Norwegian interests are safeguarded

[1417] This is how the Armed Forces carry out their mission in line with Norwegian security interests

[1418] The Armed Forces must continuously be able to understand Norway's military strategic environment, and actively contribute to shaping the environment and actors in such a way that Norwegian security interests can be pursued and promoted

[1419] The Armed Forces must continuously prevent pressure, threats, attacks and attacks against Norwegian and allied security from materializing

[1420] In this way, the Armed Forces will contribute to ensuring that attempts to harm national and allied security interests do not occur, and that armed conflict involving Norway and allies is avoided

[1421] This includes contributing to avoiding unintentional and uncontrolled escalation and loss of influence and room for manoeuvre

[1422] The Armed Forces must also be able to contribute to defending Norway or allies against enemy attacks and threats, and be able to be integrated into allied efforts

[1423] The Armed Forces' most important area of focus is Norway and its surrounding areas

[1424] The Armed Forces' efforts should be prioritized towards the north, and maritime efforts should be prioritized in particular

[1425] Norwegian strategic considerations and proximity to Russian base and patrol areas make Finnmark and adjacent sea and air areas particularly important

[1426] The structure of the armed forces must have a size and composition that enables it to educate, practice, train, participate in national operations, receive and integrate with allied forces, and contribute to operations outside Norway at the same time

[1427] Furthermore, it will be important that the Armed Forces are available to contribute to society's handling of incidents and accidents when necessary

[1428] The structure of the armed forces must possess the necessary firepower, range, mobility and endurance to provide sufficient responsiveness, flexibility and ability to meet current and future security challenges

[1429] The role of the Armed Forces in the defense of Norway is not limited to a question of functioning in war and holding out as long as possible while awaiting allied support

[1430] The defense of Norway and Norwegian interests already takes place in peacetime, and it is in this phase that Norwegian influence is greatest

[1431] It is therefore crucial to develop a defense that can act in all parts of the conflict spectrum

[1432] Alliance cooperation Collective defense within the framework of NATO is a cornerstone of Norwegian security and defense policy and for the defense of Norway

[1433] The importance of a robust and effective collective defense capability has increased in line with the negative security policy developments in Europe

[1434] This implies increased emphasis on credible and effective deterrence in the alliance, while at the same time there is an increased risk of conflict and use of the allied defense capability

[1435] National defense plans are closely integrated into NATO's plans and concepts, and the Armed Forces' own capabilities, together with NATO's overall capabilities, provide military strength and credibility

[1436] Our NATO membership enables credible deterrence and defense against actors that could affect Norwegian security

[1437] An active alliance policy both within NATO and through bilateral and multinational frameworks is therefore very important

[1438] NATO's response and reinforcement forces and forces from close allies, as well as Norwegian force contributions abroad, are integrated components of the defense of Norway

[1439] As part of this, a demonstrated ability to cooperate and receive allied reinforcements is a prerequisite for effective deterrence and reassurance

[1440] As part of alliance solidarity, Norway must also be able to contribute substantially to collective deterrence and defense of other allies

[1441] The Armed Forces must be able to participate in a broad range of operations abroad, within an allied framework

[1442] In a tense situation or armed conflict, it may be in the Norwegian and allied interest for detached forces to continue operations outside Norway

[1443] The duality of alliance cooperation will become more prominent in the years to come

[1444] Expectations that Norway will make substantial contributions to allied operations will increase, particularly for the defense of Finland and Sweden, but also to NATO's eastern border more generally

[1445] Norwegian influence and room for action are closely linked to our ability and willingness to contribute strength to burden and risk sharing

[1446] Cooperation with allied countries, both in a bilateral and multilateral framework, supports NATO and contributes to increased defense capabilities

[1447] The ability to cooperate, and cooperate with the aim of obtaining reinforcement from close allies, is an important part of the allied dimension in the defense of Norway

[1448] Increased joint training and joint concept development between Norwegian and allied forces helps strengthen the Armed Forces' operational capability and our national defense capability, and contributes substantially to Norwegian security

[1449] To facilitate allied reinforcements, it is crucial to further develop and strengthen operational cooperation with close allies in Norway and our neighboring areas, also in peacetime

[1450] In this context, regional cooperation within an allied framework must be further developed and given a clearer role

[1451] Norway shall be a driving force for effective Nordic cooperation and integration within the framework of NATO

[1452] The armed forces are the foremost instrument for integrating Norway and allies in peacetime

[1453] Who Norway cooperates with affects the ability to prevent conflict, and it affects Norway's ability to influence allied choices when it comes to the balance between deterrence and reassurance, predictability and longtermism, and thus the stability in our immediate areas

[1454] Similarly, cooperation with actors with whom Norway will operate in peace, crisis and war should influence the concepts that form the basis for Norwegian forces

[1455] Both developments in NATO, Nordic unity in the alliance, and other allied cooperation reinforce a clearer regional dimension in the defense of Norway

[1456] Total Defence and Civil Society Norway's defence capability is not made up of the Defence Forces and alliance cooperation alone

[1457] Defense capability also depends on the will to defend among the population, the resilience of society, and civil-military cooperation

[1458] Total defense encompasses mutual support and cooperation between the defense sector and civil society related to incidents and crises in peace, crisis and war

[1459] The total defense system shall contribute to the utilization of the country's total resources within prevention, emergency planning, crisis management and consequence management, and is a framework for the use of military and civilian resources to safeguard both state and societal security

[1460] The security policy situation means that actors in total defense must be more active on a daily basis in order to jointly contribute to averting and handling threats across the entire crisis spectrum

[1461] The most important task of the total defense is to function in war

[1462] To function in war, it is crucial that the mechanisms are prepared in peace, through planning, training and rehearsal

[1463] A total defense prepared for war means that civil society must be able to provide comprehensive support to national and allied military efforts for the defense of Norway, while maintaining the basic functionality of civil society and the basic security of the population

[1464] Resilience in the population and local communities is a crucial prerequisite for the ability of total defense to function

[1465] At the same time, the Armed Forces will not be able to assist civilian authorities as in peacetime, as the Armed Forces' resources must be expected to be tied up in dealing with enemy military forces

[1466] In the first decades after the end of the Cold War, civilian support for military forces within the framework of total defense gradually received less attention

[1467] Over time, greater emphasis was placed on the fact that the Armed Forces should be able to assist civilian society in the event of incidents and crises in peacetime

[1468] The Armed Forces are a significant and very important emergency response actor for civilian society in peacetime, and steps have therefore been taken to simplify and clarify how civilian actors can request and receive assistance from the Armed Forces during unwanted incidents

[1469] The Armed Forces also perform several regular civilian tasks on a daily basis

[1470] In light of the security policy situation and the threat landscape facing Norway, the government sees a need for renewed attention to be given to war planning through all sectors emphasizing how support for military efforts for the defense of the country should be organized within the framework of the total defense concept

[1471] If necessary, society's combined resources should be mobilized to defend the existence of the state and society

[1472] This is as relevant to Norway's security today as when the concept was developed after World War II

[1473] To strengthen defense capabilities, endurance and resilience, the use of instruments from different parts of society must be well coordinated

[1474] The defense sector is responsible for the military part of the total defense

[1475] The Armed Forces and the other agencies in the defense sector shall contribute to the maintenance and development of total defense by being a driving force for cooperation with civilian actors

[1476] The Armed Forces also contribute to this through daily operations where collaboration with these actors takes place

[1477] The Ministry of Defence contributes to the maintenance and development of civil-military cooperation and total defence through overall policy development, management of the defence sector, facilitation through instructions, legislative and regulatory work and direct cooperation with other ministries with sectoral responsibility in total defence

[1478] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is responsible for coordinating civilian contributions to total defense

[1479] The development of total defense is discussed in more detail in chapter

[1480] The tasks of the Armed Forces

[1481] The tasks of the Armed Forces are the Storting's and the Government's overall mission to the Armed Forces

[1482] They express which tasks the Armed Forces must solve in order to fulfill its social mission, and with what ambition these must be solved

[1483] The tasks are derived from the security and defense policy goals and the ambition is set within the framework of the defense concept

[1484] The Armed Forces' planning, structure and operational capabilities must be developed in order to be able to solve the dimensioning tasks

[1485] The armed forces are the state's foremost means of power for safeguarding Norway's security in line with security and defense policy goals

[1486] The Armed Forces shall carry out the tasks set by the Storting, within a described level of ambition and established resource framework

[1487] The overall level of ambition for the Armed Forces' tasks is confirmed through the description of the individual tasks, including which key abilities or capabilities the Armed Forces need to solve the tasks

[1488] How the tasks are solved is described within the framework of the defense concept

[1489] The security policy situation and developments in other key framework factors place stricter demands on the ambition with which, and how, the Armed Forces solve their tasks

[1490] The wording of the tasks has therefore been updated to reflect the government's priorities and clarify what is the core of the Armed Forces' mission

[1491] The connection between national and allied efforts is crucial for the defense of Norway and the development of the Armed Forces

[1492] The Norwegian Defence Force shall be organised so that national and allied efforts provide mutually reinforcing and simultaneous effects for Norwegian security

[1493] Investment in defense capabilities must therefore support the security and defense policy goals, the defense concept, and the tasks of the Armed Forces with ambition

[1494] Tasks are dimensional for the Armed Forces

[1495] This means that the Armed Forces should primarily be organized, equipped, manned, led, trained and trained to solve these tasks

[1496] Prevent and deter pressure, threats and attacks against Norwegian and allied security based on NATO's collective defence. The most important task of the Armed Forces is to prevent and deter pressure, threats, attacks

[1497] This is done by contributing to credible deterrence based on our national defense capabilities, NATO's collective defense, and in close cooperation with allies

[1498] In this way, Norwegian authorities can prevent escalation to levels where our national freedom of action and influence are significantly reduced

[1499] The Norwegian Armed Forces, together with close allies and within the framework of NATO, shall contribute to effective deterrence so that potential aggressors do not attempt to attack national and allied security interests

[1500] Political, military and other pressures to challenge or violate our sovereignty, territorial integrity, democratic governance or political freedom of action must be countered

[1501] This involves actively preventing pressure, threats, attacks and attacks against Norwegian and allied security from materializing, also by helping to avoid unintentional and uncontrolled escalation and loss of influence and room for maneuver

[1502] Norway's freedom of action is greatest before armed conflict, and the same applies to the effect of Norwegian defense efforts

[1503] Then the national share of the defense effort is more prominent than the allied one

[1504] Norway will have the greatest influence over allied efforts in our immediate areas in peacetime and in the early phase of a conflict

[1505] NATO membership is the core of Norway's ability for credible deterrence

[1506] Credible deterrence must occur through a combination of robust internal capabilities and an active alliance policy that is predictable, long-term and conflict-preventing

[1507] The task requires a defense that is actively and visibly present in our areas of interest, that operates together with our allies and that possesses relevant and credible operational capabilities

[1508] The armed forces must have the ability to be present to establish and maintain situational awareness throughout the Norwegian immediate area

[1509] The armed forces must be prepared for continuous operations in and around Norway, and demonstrate allied unity, the ability to respond, resilience and combat power in cooperation with allied forces

[1510] The Armed Forces' contribution to conflict prevention in our local areas is not created by individual capacities, but by the Armed Forces' combined resources

[1511] The Armed Forces must therefore have the ability to conduct coordinated and concentrated efforts with multiple capacities simultaneously, even at short notice

[1512] Furthermore, the Armed Forces must be able to protect its own capabilities, including its own military facilities, its own military materiel and its own information

[1513] Visible ability to strengthen the defense of Norway contributes to effective deterrence

[1514] Allied presence in daily life, and Norway's ability to operate together with and receive allied reinforcements, is central to both deterrence and reassurance

[1515] The Armed Forces shall contribute to ensuring that allied operations in Norwegian areas are shaped to the greatest extent possible in line with Norwegian security interests

[1516] The Armed Forces shall contribute to strategic stability by acting consistently, predictably and transparently

[1517] Monitor Norwegian areas of interest and promptly notify relevant authorities of matters of importance to national and allied security. The Armed Forces must have the independent ability to conduct surveillance and intelligence in order to establish and maintain situational awareness in Norwegian areas of interest and proximity

[1518] National capacity for surveillance and situational awareness in its own immediate areas, particularly in the high north, must maintain influence and room for action

[1519] This provides a basis for influencing the environment and actors, so that Norwegian security interests can be pursued and promoted

[1520] The Armed Forces' surveillance and intelligence activities must at all times contribute to the decision-making basis for Norwegian political and military authorities

[1521] Norway must be able to effectively exchange intelligence of importance to Norway, NATO and other partner countries

[1522] The task is consistent for the Armed Forces in peace, crisis and war, and encompasses intelligence capacity throughout the Armed Forces from strategic to tactical level

[1523] The rest of the total defense and society at large are also increasingly dependent on the best possible situational awareness

[1524] At the same time, civil society and total defense will be able to become increasingly important contributors to a unified, civil-military situational understanding

[1525] The Armed Forces must continuously understand Norway's military strategic environment, establish a picture of the normal situation, and uncover, warn and establish an understanding of foreign actors' intentions and their capacity to threaten, undermine, exploit or attack Norway

[1526] Norway must be at the forefront among allies in situational awareness in the North, and be a leader in NATO in understanding and communicating Russian and Chinese developments and activities in Norway's immediate vicinity

[1527] Good intelligence and continuous situational awareness are a prerequisite for the Armed Forces and allies to be able to respond to emerging situations in an appropriate manner, and are a key contribution to good situational awareness in NATO

[1528] The higher level of tension in our immediate areas increases the importance of the Armed Forces' presence and ability to conduct surveillance and intelligence, both on our own behalf and in support of NATO

[1529] The intelligence service will contribute situational awareness and decision-making support to military and civilian Norwegian authorities and allies

[1530] The entire Armed Forces should be able to contribute by collecting, summarizing, analyzing and disseminating information

[1531] The national intelligence capacity shall also support operations at home and abroad at the operational and tactical level

[1532] The Armed Forces must also have the ability to protect and monitor their own capacities, systems and assets against foreign intelligence activity

[1541] Defend Norway and allies against threats, attacks and attacks

[1709] Leadership, command and control The Government and the Minister of Defence, supported by the Ministry of Defence, constitute the national, strategic level in the defence sector

[1710] The Chief of Defence is the government's closest professional military advisor

[1711] The Ministry of Defence exercises strategic leadership, including international government liaison, and management of the four subordinate agencies in the sector (the Norwegian Armed Forces, Defence Construction, Defence Materiel and the Norwegian Defence Research Institute), on behalf of the Minister of Defence, as well as professional management of the National Security Authority's (NSM) work related to the defence sector

[1712] The Chief of Defence has full command of Norwegian forces in peacetime and ensures leadership and operational management through the Defence Staff

[1713] The Chief of Defence delegates command and control through directives to subordinate force commanders

[1714] The Military Mission in Brussels (MMB) is the Norwegian Armed Forces' military representation at NATO Headquarters, and ensures the Norwegian Armed Forces' permanent participation in NATO's Military Committee

[1715] The Norwegian Armed Forces Operational Headquarters (FOH) is Norway's military joint operational headquarters

[1716] Operational command of the Armed Forces is delegated to the FOH

[1717] The Chief of Defence Forces leads the Armed Forces' forces and operations across all branches of defence and departments, is the Chief of Defence's advisor on military operations and contributes to the preparation of strategic advice for the use of the Armed Forces

[1718] FOH also coordinates allied operations based on bilateral and multinational agreements

[1722] FOH is currently the only joint operational headquarters in the Nordic region that is fully compatible with NATO

[1724] This means that for the duration of a NATO operation, the FOH will lead national operations and safeguard national sovereignty and influence, including coordination towards the total defense and with other NATO forces under JFC Norfolk

[1725] The further organization of FOH is adapted to developments in NATO and Nordic cooperation

[1730] JSEC) in Germany

[1918] What is a reservist

[1919] Reservists are personnel who on a daily basis have their primary work outside the Armed Forces, but who at the same time have a service obligation in the Armed Forces through conscription, through a previous employment relationship in the Armed Forces or through a service obligation contract

[1920] Former military personnel have, pursuant to Section 13 of the Defence Act, extended military service up to and including the year they turn

[1921] The Norwegian Armed Forces' force structure currently consists of approximately 50,000 reservists, of which approximately 40.500 are in the Norwegian Armed Forces

[1922] The rest are distributed throughout the Armed Forces, and most are in the Army

[1923] Reservists are personnel that the Armed Forces do not normally need in peacetime on a daily basis to carry out the Armed Forces' tasks, but who may be needed in various situations in peace, crisis and war

[1924] The reservist scheme makes it possible to obtain and utilize the overall personnel capacity and expertise in Norway that is necessary to carry out the Armed Forces' tasks in peace, crisis and war

[1925] Reservists can also be used more flexibly, such as to cover temporary needs nationally, but also in international staffs and international operations

[2073] The development towards more modern long-range weapons and more widespread use of unmanned systems places increased demands on our ability to defend against threats from the air

[2090] The development of the ability to manage air operations regionally is seen in the context of the development of the Armed Forces' operational headquarters

[2091] Air operational capabilities** Maintaining the capabilities of the F-35 fighter jets and the P-8 maritime patrol aircraft requires continuous development of the aircraft and associated weapons systems

[2093] The ability for air operations is strengthened by increased access to the use of NATO's joint tanker fleet

[2094] To support a larger defense structure and increase capacity for tactical transport, medical air evacuation and support for special forces, one additional C-130 J Super Hercules transport aircraft will be acquired, in addition to the current four aircraft

[2133] A separate program will be established in the defense sector in 2024 that will have overall responsibility for ensuring that the overall effects of the various air defense projects and development cycles are realized, with the assumptions based on this long-term plan. **4.8 The Home Guard** **Status and overall development** The Home Guard (HV) is the Armed Forces' nationwide territorial, land military force in support of joint operational and allied efforts in defense of Norway

[2134] The Home Guard contributes to asserting Norwegian sovereignty and defending Norwegian territory by safeguarding territorial responsibility in peace, crisis and war through local knowledge and presence throughout the country

[2135] The Home Guard currently consists of eleven Home Guard districts with district headquarters and an area structure

[2136] The total number of Home Guard soldiers is 40,500, distributed in Home Guard areas and task forces

[2137] The Home Guard's security of military and civilian objects helps maintain important societal functions in times of crisis and war

[2138] The Home Guard has an important role in total defense through coordination and cooperation with civilian authorities at regional and local levels

[2139] A united Nordic region in NATO strengthens Norway's role in receiving and supporting the movement of allied units and materiel to and through Norway

[2140] This also entails an expanded responsibility for the Home Guard

[2141] As part of the defense pledge, the government is increasing the volume, equipment, and combat power of the Home Guard

[2142] The government's initiative builds on the ongoing development of the Home Guard

[2143] The number of soldiers in the area structure has been increased and new vehicles have been added to the Home Guard, and the ability for surveillance and control has been strengthened

[2144] The Home Guard must be further developed in order to meet a demanding security policy situation

[2145] The Home Guard constitutes a resource-efficient and relevant force in the new threat landscape

[2146] The government will increase the Norwegian Armed Forces' ability to manage and plan, new capabilities will be added and the force structure will be increased

[2147] Operational ambition** The Home Guard shall contribute to the defense of Norway with a nationwide, land military presence and situational awareness

[2148] Through territorial operations, the HV will establish a presence, conduct object and area security, support allied reception, and protect logistics lines and troop movements

[2149] The HV must have the ability to engage in combat and combat smaller enemy forces throughout the country

[2150] The Norwegian Defence Force must quickly provide departments and personnel to guard and secure prioritized military and civilian objects and have sufficient capability to protect critical infrastructure, especially against complex threats in peacetime

[2151] The Home Guard should be able to protect objects along the coastline

[2152] The Norwegian Armed Forces play a central role in total defense in peace, crisis and war and are a relevant emergency resource in support of civil society

[2153] Development direction and priorities** The Home Guard's ability to safeguard an expanded national territorial responsibility is being further developed

[2154] Given the increased need to secure the Armed Forces' departments, bases and infrastructure also against complex threats, it is recommended to strengthen the Norwegian Defence Force's ability to handle an increased and broader set of challenges

The combat system in the Armed Forces' Special Forces consists of the Marinejegerkommandoen, the Armed Forces' Special Command and the helicopter unit 339 SOAS

[2208] The new helicopter type will increase the ability to deploy and tactically transport own and allied forces, increase the ability to conduct special forces operations across the entire spectrum of conflicts, and meet key NATO requirements. **4.9.2 The Norwegian Armed Forces Logistics Organization** **Status and overall development** The Norwegian Armed Forces Logistics Organization (FLO) has overall responsibility for logistics in the defense sector

The Norwegian Armed Forces Medical Service (FSAN) is responsible for medical and veterinary services in the Norwegian Armed Forces, contributes with independent medical capacities and is intended to strengthen the resilience of other medical capacities in the Norwegian Armed Forces
