Total Defence encompasses mutual support and cooperation between the defence sector and civil society, related to incidents and crises across the entire spectrum, from peace to security policy crises and war

[2400] The government will further develop a total defense that is more active in daily life and is prepared for war

[2401] The development of the civilian side of total defense is taking place along several tracks, which include strengthening the population's resilience, building robust local communities, strengthening the ability to protect the civilian population, strengthening the ability to maintain critical societal functions, and strengthening the ability to support the military defense of Norway

[2402] In this context, reference is also made to the government's upcoming Total Emergency Preparedness Report

[2403] Support within the framework of total defense for handling crises in peacetime usually goes from the Armed Forces to civilian society

[2404] The role of the Armed Forces in the rescue efforts after the landslide in Gjerdrum, extensive assistance to civil authorities during the corona pandemic, and assistance to the police in securing critical infrastructure after the sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines are among recent examples of this

[2405] The Armed Forces also assist civil authorities in handling incidents and crises abroad

[2406] The Armed Forces have good preparedness and ability to assist civilian authorities in peacetime

[2407] In crisis and war, support within the framework of total defense will primarily go in the opposite direction, from civil society to Norwegian and allied military efforts

[2408] The ability to support military forces requires planning and adaptation already in peacetime, in all sectors with responsibility in total defense

[2409] An increasingly high pace of operations means that the defense sector and allies need more frequent civilian support, also in connection with daily operations in peacetime

[2410] At the same time, the Armed Forces must continue to be able to assist civil society in the face of both accidental and intentional incidents

[2411] Support and cooperation in daily life are valuable for the total defense's ability to function even in the upper parts of the crisis spectrum

[2412] Both civil society support for daily operations and the Armed Forces' assistance for civilian crisis management contribute to increased cooperation and closer relationships between total defense actors, and better mutual knowledge of each other's needs

[2413] This supports the ability of the same actors to find each other and function together even in war

[2414] The current total defense concept was adopted through the Storting's consideration

[2415] No. 42 (2003–2004), cf. Recommendation

[2416] P. no. 234 and St. report

[2417] No. 39 (2003–2004), cf. Recommendation

[2418] Prop. No. 49 (2004–

[2419] Research and development (R&D) activities support a functioning total defense across the entire crisis spectrum

[2420] This is discussed in more detail in Chapter 10. The overall consequences for society of any acts of war on Norwegian territory are expected to be significant

[2421] Both civilian and military lives could be lost, and the destruction of infrastructure and the environment could be extensive

[2422] At the same time, the need for resources for a military defense campaign will be significant, and much of the additional military needs will have to be covered by civilian society

[2423] There will also be a particular need for civilian support for military forces in crisis and war

[2424] Early reception and deployment of allied units to Norway, Finland and Sweden requires efforts from both the defense sector and civilian sectors

[2425] National and allied forces will need support to conduct operations over time, on and from Norwegian territory

[2426] Norway's ability to support its own and allied military efforts across the entire spectrum of crises contributes to combat power and credible deterrence, thereby supporting NATO as a credible and effective guarantor of the security of allies

[2427] A total defense prepared for war also contributes to an increased overall ability to handle threats lower on the crisis spectrum

[2428] The Government wants to ensure that all sectors with responsibility for total defense have plans for support to military forces in crisis and war, and that the sectors take military needs into account in their preparedness

[2429] Providing support to military forces is a social responsibility that applies to all sectors, agencies and actors, private as well as public

[2430] This requires civilian knowledge of military needs

[2431] Military needs for civil support are derived from the military planning for the defense of Norway

[2432] Information about these needs is currently communicated primarily from the Armed Forces to security-cleared personnel on the civilian side

[2433] At the same time, there is a need for information about military needs for civilian support to flow to all necessary levels in civilian sectors to a greater extent than is currently the case

[2434] It is also necessary that military needs are communicated concretely and at the right time, so that the information can be included as part of the planning basis and priorities in the various sectors

[2435] The Government will therefore establish regular routines that ensure that military needs for civilian support are communicated as concretely as possible to ministries with sectoral responsibility in the overall defence

[2436] The Ministry of Defense will determine what this routine should be

[2437] The government has strengthened coordination at the ministerial level related to total defense

[2438] Meetings in the Contact Group for Total Defence, which is chaired alternately by the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, have contributed to a common understanding of the situation and cross-sectoral coordination at the ministry level

[2439] The Government will provide common priorities for this work across sectors

[2440] A total defense prepared for war means that work on supporting military defense must be prioritized and resourced in peacetime by all sectors with responsibility for total defense

[2441] The Government will therefore annually set common priorities for this work across sectors

[2442] The most important task of the Armed Forces is to prevent and deter pressure, threats, attacks and threats by contributing to credible deterrence based on NATO's collective defence and in close cooperation with allies

[2443] Total defense actors must therefore also be able to support national and allied military efforts on a daily basis, for example during exercises in Norway. Exercising and training civil-military cooperation is crucial for support and cooperation within the framework of total defense to function as intended across the entire crisis spectrum and at all levels

[2444] Military exercises in Norway in themselves involve relevant training for a number of actors in civilian sectors

[2445] In connection with a field exercise, civilian actors take care of the responsibilities they already have in their daily lives, for example related to border control and traffic management

[2446] In addition, field exercises provide opportunities for practicing civilian support for military forces in various areas, and are a good framework for testing the various sectors' contingency plans

[2447] Staff and desk exercises in the defense sector also provide opportunities for relevant exercises of civilian support to military forces and civilian sectors' own exercise objectives

[2448] The Government will therefore further facilitate the training of total defense actors within the framework of military exercises

[2449] Civilian actors must, when relevant, prioritize exercise participation also from the part of the organization that does not work with the defense sector on a daily basis

[2450] Field exercises must, in addition to being handled as incidents, be used as a framework for practicing one's own activities

[2451] Civilian actors must be involved in the Armed Forces' exercise planning at an early stage to align expectations for civilian participation, resource allocation, and facilitate exercise benefits for civilian actors as well

[2452] This involves prioritizing which military exercises civilian participation provides the best training benefits, to avoid inappropriate dispersion of resources

[2453] Following civil-military exercises, sufficient resources must be allocated in both the civilian and military sectors for evaluation and follow-up of learning points

[2454] Total defense actors must prioritize training the breadth of their own organization, including decision-makers, in scenarios where civilian sectors must provide support to military forces, while at the same time maintaining basic services to the population at an adequate level

[2455] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security's responsibility for coordinating civilian contributions to total defense includes planning and conducting national exercises in the civilian sector in collaboration with other ministries

[2456] The government has already taken steps to ensure that exercises and training on the civilian and military sides are seen in greater context, and that good arenas for training within the framework of total defense are identified and utilized. Military requisition Military authorities have broad powers to requisition resources under the Requisition Act

[2457] The law gives military authorities the ability to requisition directly in war, but also the right to issue advance requisitions in peacetime

[2458] The Ministry of Defence will, in collaboration with affected ministries and their sectors, ensure that the Armed Forces continue their work to have an overview of the resources needed in a force-building phase or armed conflict

[2459] In 2022, the Norwegian Armed Forces resumed the scheme of annual issuance of advance requisitions, and has established a digital database that contributes to an overview of resources throughout the country

[2460] Mapping resources in peacetime through the interconnection and use of already existing public registers helps ensure that the Armed Forces have an overview of necessary resources, and that their use is coordinated in advance and, to the greatest extent possible, coordinated with civilian authorities

[2461] The continued work on mapping and advance requisitions contributes to ensuring that total defense actors and private individuals are prepared

[2462] Transition to cut greenhouse gas emissions affects access

[2463] The Armed Forces have certain resources from civil society

[2464] For example, electrification on roads, railways, in the air and at sea can affect which resources are suitable for use by the Armed Forces in war

[2465] The Norwegian Armed Forces will implement significant measures to reduce the sector's greenhouse gas emissions and adapt the sector to a changed climate

[2466] With today's technology, shifting away from fossil fuels creates new vulnerabilities

[2467] The defense sector must understand and decide how this transition can be implemented without compromising the Defense's ability to perform its tasks

[2468] In its further work on requisitioning, the Armed Forces will assess what requirements for deliveries, production and inventory can be placed on business actors

[2469] Both the Emergency Preparedness Act and the Military Requisition Act can be used for this purpose

[2470] The work will be done in collaboration with affected ministries, underlying sectors and affected business actors

[2471] The use of requisitioning should be avoided where deliveries can be secured through cooperation with the relevant industries. The Government assumes that councils and committees used for crisis management in peacetime should also play a role in crisis and armed conflict

[2472] The ministerial level will meet in the Crisis Council, and much of the coordination at the ministerial level will take place directly between the ministries and within the framework of the Contact Group for Total Defence

[2475] STF consists of representatives from the Armed Forces and a number of civilian organizations with responsibility for total defense

[2476] The Ministry of Defence, in collaboration with affected ministries, is assessing whether the STF's mandate should be changed to strengthen the body's role in total defence, and whether the STF can better facilitate participation from the business community, which possesses expertise, services and physical resources on which Norway and total defence depend

[2477] Also at the regional and local level, there are various cooperation and emergency preparedness bodies where both civilian and military actors are represented, for example, county emergency preparedness councils and municipal emergency preparedness councils

[2478] Active civil-military cooperation in peacetime at all levels supports a total defense prepared for war

[2510] International law of war and the use of civilians** The defense sector is increasingly using competitive bidding and strategic cooperation to solve tasks that were previously assigned to the Armed Forces

[2511] This means increased use and dependence on civilian actors to perform critical tasks in the operation of the Armed Forces, also in a war or crisis situation

[2512] As a result, it is important that, among other things, international law aspects of competitive bidding and the use of strategic cooperation are explained, so that Norway does not violate international law when using these

[2513] The international law of war and national legislation, such as guidelines from the Ministry of Defence and internal regulations in the Armed Forces, set the framework for the use of military force

[2514] The use of civilians to support military operations in armed conflict is, with certain limitations, permitted under the international law of war

[2515] Planning for, and training in, civilian support in armed conflict must be in accordance with the international law of war

[2516] The Ministry of Defense has in Prop

[2517] S (2023–2024) responded to the Storting's request resolution no. 133, 1 December 2020 (Recommendation

[2518] S (2020–2021)) on the use of non-military personnel and matters related to the international law of war

[2519] The government has emphasized that Norway must comply with its international obligations by having good routines and guidelines for the defense sector's use of civilians in a possible war situation

[2520] In parallel with responding to the request decision, the Ministry of Defence has prepared an international law study to help clarify the principles and overarching international law rules related to the limits on the use of civilians in war

[2521] The report is intended as guidance and an interpretative statement on the international legal framework for the use of civilian employees in the Armed Forces, civilians from the total defense, and civilian contractors and suppliers in support of the Armed Forces in wartime

[2522] The report will be sent to the agencies in the defense sector in

[2523] Along with the report, an assignment will be issued to the defense sector to conduct a survey to gain an overview of the current use of civilians, and what measures may need to be implemented to ensure that the defense sector complies with international law

[2524] Examples of measures could be that the Armed Forces must be able to equip civilian personnel who support the defense effort with necessary equipment such as uniforms

[2525] The results of this survey will guide the implementation of measures. Access to sufficient manpower in a war situation may be challenging, and the government may need to prioritize civilian labor resources across sectors

[2526] On January 15, 2024, the government submitted for consultation a proposal for a new chapter in the Civil Protection Act on civil workforce preparedness

[2527] The proposal includes a legal basis for a future regulation on civilian work obligation in a security crisis or war

[2528] Anyone who is imposed with a civilian work obligation under the proposal will not be able to be required to perform work that, under international law, entails the status of a combatant

[2529] The Armed Forces' exemption scheme regulates exemption from military service in war, when war threatens and during force buildup

[2530] More about the exemption scheme in Chapter 7. Resilience across the breadth of civil society is important for Norway's overall ability to resist attack

[2531] This means that the entire society must be mentally and physically prepared for the fact that hostilities on Norwegian territory will result in a significant absence of the services and resources they are accustomed to in peacetime

[2532] Self-preparedness, a resilient population and robust local communities, as well as robust critical infrastructure, are therefore crucial to the nation's overall ability to resist attack

[2533] Acts of war will cause civilian casualties and suffering

[2534] In war, the needs of the individual must give way to what will be the community's most important task, which is to defend Norwegian sovereignty

[2535] It is therefore important to create understanding among the population about how normal expectations of society could radically change in a serious security crisis or war

[2536] The work on resilience in society's critical civil functions is linked to four main tasks

[2537] To maintain state governance and crisis management, to support military efforts, to maintain basic services to the population and to protect the civilian population through civil protection measures

[2538] Civilian sectors must therefore plan to handle these four tasks simultaneously

[2539] Civil preparedness must also be based on the fact that in times of crisis and war, the Armed Forces will be tied down to solving military tasks and have limited capacity to assist civilian authorities

[2540] The Government has decided to strengthen national work on NATO's Seven Baseline Requirements for resilience in critical civil society functions

[2541] Service obligation for civilian employees in the Defence Sector New Section 25a of the Defence Act entered into force on 1 January

[2542] The legal basis allows the Ministry of Defence and subordinate agencies to enter into contracts regarding service obligations with civilian employees in their own operations

[2543] After entering into a contract for service obligations, the businesses can dispose of the personnel

[2544] The purpose of a contractual service obligation is to legislate that civilian employees in the defense sector have an obligation to report to work and perform their work even in war and when war is threatened

[2545] Until a contract for service obligation has been entered into, civilian employees may have the right and obligation to interrupt their work if there is a danger to life and health, cf. the Working Environment Act, section 2-3, second paragraph, letter

[2546] The use of civilians who have entered into a contract of service under Section 25a must be seen in the context of the rules and requirements of the international law of war

[2547] A resilient population and resilient local communities are in themselves an important prerequisite for civil society's ability to support the military defense of Norway

[2548] Resilient communities will have a better ability to take care of themselves when unwanted events occur

[2549] A resilient society and critical infrastructure have fewer vulnerabilities that threat actors will be able to exploit

[2550] This in turn means that there are more and better resources that can be used to support military efforts

[2551] The work of strengthening resilience must already take place in peacetime so that society is as well prepared as possible for crisis and war

[2552] NATO's "Seven Baseline Requirements"** Security of continuity of national governance systems and critical public services Robust energy supply

[2553] Ability to handle uncontrolled movements of people

[2554] Robust food and water supply

[2555] Ability to handle mass casualties

[2556] Robust communication systems Robust transport systems The Armed Forces assist civil society within the framework of the Armed Forces' mission

[2557] The assistance is provided at the request of civilian authorities when civil society resources are not sufficient, available or appropriate

[2558] This applies, for example, to natural disasters, accidents and serious criminal acts such as terrorism

[2718] The government's approach to currency risk follows the self-insurer principle

[2719] Effective with the 2022 budget, a system was introduced for the defense budget that involves currency adjustment of all investments with a cost limit higher than NOK 1 billion in the annual budget processes

[2720] This has been a well-functioning risk-reducing measure for the defense sector, and has contributed to increased predictability, especially during a period of steadily weakening krone exchange rates

[2721] Overall, the scheme has provided extraordinary compensation to the defense budget of NOK 5 billion during the period

[2722] The absence of a scheme like this would have resulted in reduced purchasing power, imbalance in the plan and consequences for defense capability

[2723] In the event of a strengthening of the krone exchange rate, the scheme provides for a corresponding reduction in the defense budget

[2724] The purpose is to maintain the defense sector's purchasing power over time, regardless of fluctuations in the exchange rate of the Norwegian krone against other relevant currencies

[2725] The government will continue the current currency adjustment scheme

[2726] The scheme does not include investments with a cost limit of less than NOK 1 billion or operating items

[2729] These agreements are an integral part of larger procurements of military equipment such as aircraft and helicopters

[2799] The education reform (URE) was a structural and quality reform that was implemented in the period

[2800] The reform contained a number of organizational changes that were intended to provide better conditions for quality in education while reducing expenses

[2801] The need to adapt the education system to the new system for military employees (OMT) and the university and college reform was central

[2802] Furthermore, the reform was to free up approximately 560 million 2017 kroner for operational activities annually

[2803] This was to be done, among other things, by reducing or removing overlapping management elements, support functions and expertise environments

[2804] The most important organizational changes in the reform were that the Defence Staff was given overall responsibility for management and control of the education system; one joint college was established with responsibility for all level-forming education, and the weapons schools were merged into one school environment in each branch of defence

[2805] In addition, a number of measures were taken to consolidate functions and create more common, needs-based and harmonized education

[2806] The Ministry of Defense, with support from the Armed Forces, evaluated the education reform

[2807] The evaluation concluded that the reform has moved the education system in the desired direction and that most of the objectives of the education reform had been achieved

[2808] At the same time, development areas related to governance of the education system, robust academic environments and educational quality were identified

[2809] These are followed up by the Armed Forces in the further development of the education system

[2810] As part of this work, the government is prioritizing that it will be possible to apply for the Armed Forces' education through Coordinated Admissions, and that the quality of the education will be evaluated using the Study Barometer

The defense sector is generally recruiting well, but there are challenges in certain areas

The Government emphasizes recognition, care and follow-up of personnel before, during and after service in international operations

[3034] Veterans from international operations have served Norway in war-torn and crisis-affected areas

[3035] In total, more than 100,000 people have served in more than 100 operations

[3084] The Defence Pledge – for Norway's security. The defence sector shall make procurement faster. The defence sector shall grow

[3085] This means that more material, ICT and infrastructure that the sector needs must be provided, at the right time and in sufficient volume

[3086] Over time, the defense sector has developed strict requirements for management and control, with good and trust-building procurement processes

[3087] At the same time, this has contributed to procurement taking a long time and requiring large resources

[3088] In a heightened security situation, this is no longer sufficient

[3089] There is a need to procure materials faster and in larger volumes

[3090] Procurement processes must be further developed and adapted to the complexity and risk of individual projects

[3091] Norway and our allies are experiencing challenges in procuring materiel and ammunition

[3092] The war in Ukraine has led to high demand, long lead times and high price inflation

[3093] It is likely that price inflation will persist and increase

[3094] The war in Ukraine has also shown that the production capacity for defense equipment in the West is too small

[3095] This creates great uncertainty about the time it takes to get new equipment in place

[3096] The Government will work to ensure that procurements are carried out more quickly, within available financial limits and with sufficient volume

[3097] The defense of the future must take climate and environmental considerations into account to a greater extent

[3098] Procurement processes must take into account the impact on the climate and environment, and be able to handle new requirements as a result of climate change

[3099] The Government will establish governance models that combine the need for management and control with new requirements for speed and volume

[3100] In addition, procurement expertise in the sector will be strengthened

[3101] Better ability to innovate, improve and streamline will also contribute to better procurement (cf. chap

[3102] The Government will strengthen the national defense industry, increase production capacity and enter into binding cooperation with allies on the acquisition of important capabilities. The need for faster procurement and larger volumes places new demands on the defense sector's procurement processes

[3103] Therefore, the Government will facilitate adapted procurement processes, where the consideration of faster implementation is weighed against the risk this entails for proper implementation

[3104] For example, consideration should be given to simplifying or adapting processes that apply to materiel that the Armed Forces or close allies already have experience with

[3105] Adaptations can also be considered when upgrading existing systems where suppliers are largely given, but also when procuring new main systems for the Armed Forces

[3106] Such flexible implementation can result in shorter investment processes and lower implementation costs

[3107] The defense sector must make the most efficient use of community resources

[3108] The risk of error makes it necessary to conduct thorough assessments with each individual acquisition

[3109] There are currently requirements for the assessment, planning and quality assurance of government investment projects with an estimated total cost of over one billion kroner

[3110] For digitalization projects, this applies to projects of over NOK 300 million

[3111] This practice is well established in the defense sector and will be continued

[3112] There is room for simplifications and adjustments in procurement processes, which could lead to faster implementation

[3113] Before time-consuming investigations are initiated, it must be assessed whether there is a need and basis for making simplifications and adjustments to the procurement processes

[3114] The benefits of faster implementation must be weighed against the risk of misinvestment

[3115] The processes must be implemented properly, and both contribute to ensuring that the procurement delivers the planned defense capability at the right time and that the sector's resources are utilized efficiently

[3116] The Government wants considerations of timely procurement to be a central part of the defense sector's procurement processes

[3117] This places greater demands on flexibility in implementation

[3118] The regulations that apply to various procurements depend, among other things, on whether they are particularly important for Norway's security, whether they are procurements in collaboration with other nations, or whether they are open or restricted tenders

[3119] There are various exemption provisions that can be used, if defined conditions are met

[3120] Where it can result in adapted and shorter investigation and procurement processes, or is considered important for Norway's security, the use of these opportunities must be carefully considered

[3121] Long procurement processes and long lead times contribute to increasing the cost and delaying procurement

[3122] To strengthen the ability to carry out procurement in the defense sector, the government will propose raising the threshold for when the defense sector must go to the Storting for approval

[3123] For large material projects, the government will propose raising this limit from NOK 500 million to NOK 1 billion, for the effective implementation of prioritized measures for rapid strengthening of defense capabilities

[3124] For large property, building and construction projects, proposals will be made to raise the limit from NOK 200 million to NOK 500 million for more efficient implementation of prioritized measures

[3125] This will result in faster processes as more projects and more measures can be fast-tracked, thereby contributing to an increased pace of procurement and development

[3126] When making major investment decisions, external professional groups usually also conduct quality assurance of the projects

[3127] The purpose of this is to assist the government with an independent assessment

[3128] This is important and strengthens the government's decision-making basis

[3129] In cases where rapid assessment and decision-making processes are critically important, considerations for Norway's security must weigh heavily and consideration must be given to how procurement processes can be shortened and simplified, including differentiating processes for different material categories

[3130] In projects where it is obvious that there are no more alternatives, there may be grounds for granting exceptions for early investigation of the project and quality assurance of concept selection

[3131] Examples of when this has been provided in the past are major upgrade projects of existing infrastructure or when repurchasing donated equipment to solve short-term needs

[3132] Action should be taken to get more for your money** Greater responsibility for the community's resources also entails a great responsibility to get the most for the resources made available

[3133] This is even more important in a period when the price of military equipment has increased

[3134] The Government will follow up to ensure that the resources now made available are used in a way that provides the greatest possible operational capability for the money

[3135] This means that the defense sector must negotiate better and use more suppliers to reduce costs and delivery times

[3136] The defense sector should prioritize what is "good enough" and that delivers in terms of quality, price and volume

[3137] Where cheaper or faster alternative solutions exist, these should be thoroughly assessed. The ability to carry out procurement is strengthened The need for extensive investments and rapid implementation also places greater demands on the implementation capacity in the sector

[3138] The investment environments in Defence Materiel, Defence Construction and the Armed Forces must recruit and retain personnel with relevant experience and expertise

[3139] At the same time, it will be important to find better solutions with the resources that have already been allocated

[3140] The defense sector's investigations must continue to be carried out with good quality

[3141] In a period where the Armed Forces will grow rapidly, it will be important to help ensure that decision-making processes proceed as quickly as possible

[3142] The defense is entering the 2020s, and the government will pay particular attention to ensuring that approved development projects are implemented according to plan and as quickly as possible

[3143] Procurement shall be made in cooperation with allies** The Government's commitment to the Armed Forces means that several large material systems shall be procured in cooperation with allies

[3144] Large-scale production and joint purchasing of ready-made solutions can help make procurement faster and cheaper

[3145] Norway has proven to be a reliable and sought-after partner in large material procurements

[3146] The F-35 cooperation and the acquisition of P-8 maritime patrol aircraft, and new submarines are examples of successful collaborative projects with important allies such as the United States and Germany

[3147] The experience from these projects must be utilized when entering into new partnerships for large material procurements

[3148] At the same time, it is important that established collaborations do not prevent the search for alternative solutions that can lead to lower costs, shorter delivery times, or increased endurance. More off-the-shelf products and similar materials to our allies should be procured More procurements and investments should also be made based on materials that are already available on the market

[3149] Over time, it has been a challenge that special adaptations, which make the equipment unique for Norwegian use, lead to increased costs and longer lead times

[3150] The special adaptations have also led to challenges in obtaining spare parts or disproportionately high costs for updating and maintenance

[3151] The government assumes that the least possible customization is key to ensuring the fastest possible deliveries at the most favorable price

[3152] Purchasing off-the-shelf products contributes to lower lifetime costs because economies of scale help lower the price of spare parts and maintenance throughout the systems' lifetime

[3153] A greater proportion of procurement of fully developed equipment that other allies use will make joint operational cooperation easier

[3154] It will also help reduce maintenance and acquisition costs, as more people purchase the same system and spare parts, which in turn reduces unit costs

[3155] To ensure that more off-the-shelf and similar equipment is procured as our allies, the government will provide strategic guidance in an early phase of ongoing and upcoming procurement projects

[3156] Early collaboration with industry and with allied nations is important to reduce implementation time

[3157] ICT in the defense sector. The changing security situation emphasizes the importance of ICT for Norway's security and defense capabilities

[3158] Although many measures have been implemented, the defense sector faces challenges in reaping the benefits

[3159] The reasons for this are several

[3160] Both the Svendsen Committee and the Office of the Auditor General's Doc 3:3 (2022–2023) pointed to the importance of governance and expertise

[3161] These challenges have been highlighted in a number of studies

[3162] Work on the management and competence challenges in the ICT area in the defense sector is underway

[3163] A new governance model for ICT will help limit the fragmentation of roles, responsibilities and authority between the Ministry of Defence and the agencies, and between the agencies

[3164] This involves, among other things, a consolidation of the development, operation and maintenance of the Armed Forces' secure platforms (FSP) in the Armed Forces

[3165] Work will continue with the implementation of a new management model in other parts of the ICT area. ICT solutions in the defense sector will be designed to a greater extent from a user perspective

[3166] This is important for effective use and problem solving in a normal situation, and becomes even more important in crisis and war

[3167] If different ICT infrastructures are to be able to interact and be usable across the entire conflict spectrum, systems and applications must be available where users are, have a user interface that users know and can operate, systems and applications must be able to interact, and there must be the greatest possible similarity in user experiences across systems

[3168] Data and digitalization must be integrated elements in ICT projects so that ICT solutions and architecture support real user needs

[3169] Digitization and the utilization of data as a basis for decisions, management and prioritization must generally be placed much higher on the agenda

[3170] Reduced usability and lack of interoperability in these areas will reduce the ability to respond to incidents

[3171] The Norwegian Armed Forces' program "Mime" is ongoing and aims to increase the operational capability of the Norwegian Armed Forces and thereby strengthen the Norwegian Armed Forces' ability to perform all its tasks

[3172] This is achieved through the ability for digital interaction, efficient use of resources and management of operations at the tactical level, in joint operational cooperation with national and allied forces

[3173] Improving the Norwegian Armed Forces' digital foundation involves, among other things, modernizing data centers, FSP, core solutions for administrative ICT such as the joint integrated management system (FIF) and associated application portfolio, as well as communication infrastructure (FKI) and graded network

[3174] Improving host nation support in the NATO context and strengthening defensive cyber capabilities are other priority areas

[3175] The defense sector is facing a significant transformation within the ICT area

[3176] Particularly important for success in this is improved management of ICT in the sector, improved ICT competence at all levels, appropriate use of the market, and not least close cross-sectoral cooperation to achieve synergies by establishing robust capabilities

[3177] Implementation and follow-up of climate and environmental requirements in defense sector procurement** The defense sector shall use its purchasing power to reduce negative climate and environmental impacts

[3178] Where possible, it should also promote climate- and environmentally friendly solutions

[3179] As a significant market player, the defense sector has the opportunity to influence its suppliers

[3180] This can help ensure that climate- and environmentally friendly solutions that are in line with the Armed Forces' operational needs are prioritized

[3181] Procurement in the defense sector should therefore contribute to the defense sector reducing its negative climate and environmental impact

[3182] The defense sector's procurement regulations will also be updated to take greater account of climate and the environment

[3183] All public procurement processes must, as a general rule, give climate and environmental considerations a minimum of 30 percent weight when awarding a supplier

[3184] Alternatively, climate and environmental requirements can be set in the requirements specification, if it is clear that this will provide a better climate and environmental effect

[3185] These rules basically also apply to the defense sector, although the sector has certain exceptions

[3186] The procurement regulations for the defense sector (ARF) are now being updated, which also includes increased consideration of climate and the environment in line with the intentions of the public procurement regulations

[3187] The Norwegian Armed Forces' project model for procurement is also being updated with the goal of including good tools for taking climate and environmental considerations into account

[3188] To enable the sector to formulate good award criteria and requirements for climate and the environment, there is a need for several different forms of expertise

[3189] Expertise in how requirements and award criteria are formulated, measured and followed up is a prerequisite for the intention of the procurement regulations to be fulfilled

[3191] The Government will facilitate increased production and development of a stronger defense industry and defense technology in Norway

[3192] Norway's defense industrial strategy is based on the

[3193] S (2020–2021) to Report

[3194] Cooperation for security – National defense industrial strategy for a high-tech and future-oriented defense

[3195] The government wants to create a foundation for a more robust defense industry and has three main goals

[3196] – Increased resilience, security of supply and national preparedness – A stronger and more robust national industrial base – Active and targeted participation in international material and R&D cooperation

[3197] The Government will present a further developed strategy for the defense industry based on Meld

[3198] St. 17 (2020–2021), but also the goals and frameworks presented below. Increased resilience, security of supply and national preparedness

[3199] It is a growing challenge to meet our own and our allies' needs for defense equipment

[3200] Norway has a responsibility to help meet demand

[3201] Increased industrial capacity in Norway and among allies is absolutely necessary to maintain deterrence in NATO and support Ukraine's defense struggle

[3202] It is also crucial for increasing the Armed Forces' endurance, security of supply and preparedness

[3203] The war in Ukraine and the deteriorating security situation in Europe have clearly shown that the production capacity of the Western defense industry is insufficient

[3204] Western allies and partner countries have donated surplus equipment and much of the equipment in their own structures to Ukraine

[3205] In order to maintain support for Ukraine and at the same time build up its own preparedness and defense capabilities, Norway and other Western countries are dependent on increased production in the defense industry

[3206] Russia has strengthened its defense industry production by converting to a war economy, while also having partner countries that, among other things, support the country's ammunition needs

[3207] The West has so far been unable to increase production in line with what the security situation dictates

[3208] This is due to a long-term downscaled and market-adapted production capacity, combined with open world trade that leads to vulnerabilities in value and supply chains in the form of restrictions on access to raw materials, components and other input factors

[3209] The European defense industry is fragmented along national lines, making it challenging to achieve a coordinated increase in production capacity

[3210] The government has already taken measures to help increase production capacity in the defense industry

[3211] The industry itself has also taken measures to increase capacity and better meet the increased demand

[3212] The government's contribution to strengthening the defense industry's production capability includes, among other things

[3213] – Agreement with Nammo AS to produce artillery ammunition for NOK 1.95 billion to meet national needs

[3215] – Joint Scandinavian initiative in which Norway has entered into an agreement with Nammo AS for the delivery of artillery ammunition to Ukraine

[3216] Norway's share is NOK 200 million out of a total framework of approximately NOK 600 million

[3217] – Norwegian participation with 190 million kroner in the EU program ASAP, which will help increase the production of ammunition

[3218] – Co-financing of Norwegian companies' ASAP projects of NOK 950 million

[3219] ASAP grants will trigger billions in investments in production capacity for ammunition, missiles and explosives

[3220] – Up to 2 billion kroner to increase production capacity in the Norwegian defense industry, of which 1 billion kroner will be used for concrete measures to increase production capacity at Nammo AS

[3221] – Up to approximately NOK 940 million for pre-ordering of components with long lead times to accelerate the upgrade of the NASAMS air defense system and the planned development of its own air defense structure

[3257] Stronger and more robust national industrial base

[3258] The defense sector constantly needs to acquire, update and further develop everything from aircraft and tanks, to uniforms and small arms

[3259] All of these acquisitions require technological insight and operational understanding to make the right choice

[3260] For large and complex systems, the industrial base is often a relatively small and transparent group of suppliers with whom the defense sector has an established dialogue

[3261] In many cases, it makes procurement easier to handle

[3262] A market with few players also entails a significant risk of increased prices and can lead to long delivery times

[3268] Strategic partnerships with industry and business The Government will use strategic agreements as a tool

[3269] Strategic agreements are long-term and mutually binding collaborations between the defense sector and actors in the business community

[3270] The agreements should not replace tasks

[3271] The defense should do it, but supplement it

[3272] These are agreements that have special significance for national preparedness and security, and encompass cooperation in peace, crisis and war with clearly defined responsibilities and roles

[3273] Such agreements are intended to strengthen the Armed Forces' operational capability, contribute to national security of supply, strengthen the capacity for allied reception, ensure preparedness and streamline logistics

[3274] Strategic cooperation with Norwegian industry and business will contribute to security of supply and strengthened preparedness through national long-term access to necessary goods and services

[3275] Where the Armed Forces' needs cannot be met by the Armed Forces themselves, strategic agreements can contribute to flexible capacity increases

[3276] For this to be possible, it is essential that relevant business actors maintain relevant expertise

[3277] It is therefore important that actors who should be available in times of crisis and war are also used in times of peace

[3278] Strategic collaboration with Norwegian industry and business should be done in a way that provides a common understanding of roles, responsibilities and obligations

[3350] The government will also prioritize the development of infrastructure used for allied reception

[3351] Management, operation and maintenance of the property portfolio will become more efficient, and the ability to implement projects within the planned time, cost and performance will improve

[3352] The sector's construction activities must reduce their total climate footprint and negative environmental impact

[3353] There should be a holistic approach to the management of the defense sector's cultural and historical properties that ensures improved condition, use and cultural dissemination

[3354] The Government is concerned that needs are planned comprehensively and adequately funded to provide the Armed Forces with a timely and functional property portfolio

[3355] This is a fundamental prerequisite for building up the Armed Forces

[3356] Increased pace and enhanced implementation capacity in projects To support the comprehensive strengthening of the Armed Forces, construction and improvement of buildings and facilities must take place significantly faster than previously

[3357] To implement the defense pledge, the sector must adjust working methods for real estate, construction and civil engineering activities

[3358] A comprehensive plan must be prepared for the development of property, buildings and facilities at the right time, place and cost

[3359] This plan should ensure synchronization with both material plans and personnel escalation

[3360] The plan is developed in close collaboration with the agencies

[3362] This applies to Setermoen, Bardufoss, Skjold, Linderud, Wallemsviken, Kuhaugen, Terningmoen, Haakonsvern, Ørland and Porsanger

[3363] Fast decision-making chains are necessary for efficient project implementation

[3364] The scope for action in the government and defense sector project models should be better utilized with regard to simplification and fast-tracking for prioritized projects

[3381] A more efficient and sustainable management model

[3382] The management of the defence sector's building stock must be improved

[3383] The Government will strengthen maintenance of the building stock to increase operational capacity and avoid further deterioration in value

[3384] There is a need for a strong focus on maintenance to reduce the maintenance backlog

[3386] This includes clarifying roles and responsibilities in the management and organization of services

[3387] Further development of the sector's property management will require the use of better technological tools

[3388] For example, introducing a common digital system in the defense sector will ensure more efficient management, planning and production

[3390] The current solution involves too much limitation to assignment-based financing and too high a degree of internal transactions

[3391] It is important that the sector is funded so that Forsvarsbygg's role as a professional advisor to owners and users of the defence sector's property, buildings and facilities is strengthened and further developed

[3392] The changes will be based on recommendations in the review

[3393] Various adjustments to the current rent model will be considered

[3394] The government will also make better use of the property stock by using standard solutions for office and residential development

[3395] Climate and environmental measures must be implemented broadly and accurately when the property stock is renewed or old components are replaced

[3397] Review of property, building and construction management

[3398] The Government will complete a review of the management of property, buildings and facilities in the defense sector in the spring of

[3399] The purpose is to identify measures to improve resource use and more efficient, comprehensive management of the defense sector's property assets

[3401] Further development of the management of property, buildings and structures will support operational capability and preparedness, enable the sector to use and care for cultural and historical properties, and contribute to a more sustainable and simpler management model

[3402] Living and working conditions

[3403] Housing capacity in the defense sector will be increased to support the planned personnel escalation

[3404] The Armed Forces shall offer good living and working conditions to its conscripts and employees

[3405] This is important for attracting and retaining personnel, and for accommodating employees who move or commute to perform important tasks

[3406] The Government will facilitate the settlement of more people in the defense municipalities, and will particularly prioritize good living environments in the districts and integrating living environments into local communities, in collaboration with the individual municipality

[3407] The balance in the housing portfolio and accommodation capacity must reflect the real need

[3408] Whether employees in the Armed Forces move to duty stations or commute varies greatly

[3409] It is therefore important to adapt the offer to the different needs of each location

[3410] In order to realize the strengthening of the Armed Forces in a timely manner, a larger proportion of competitive buildings will be acquired via leasing and rental, so that the need for accommodation capacity can be realized quickly and with sufficient quality

[3411] This can be done in collaboration with municipalities and private actors

[3412] In this way, the need for capital investments will be reduced, and it will free up capacity at Forsvarsbygg

[3413] Where there is a local, well-functioning market, housing should preferably be rented in the market

[3414] These should have the lowest possible degree of special adaptation

[3415] What is most appropriate between owning and renting will vary depending on location, market situation and how immediate the need is

[3416] Purpose-built buildings will primarily be owned by the sector, with Defence Buildings as the primary actor

[3418] It allows development, adaptation and modernization according to defense-specific needs

[3419] However, owning one requires significant investment in operating and maintenance costs

[3420] Leased housing from private or other public entities can provide increased flexibility and reduce the need for capital investments, while the landlord is usually responsible for technical maintenance and upgrades

[3421] Increased rental share will increase the sector's operating costs

[3422] In several municipalities, the Armed Forces are a major player in the local community

[3423] The Government will facilitate vibrant defense municipalities, and will strengthen the dialogue with defense municipalities to develop good local communities where the defense sector is well integrated

[3424] It is therefore crucial to have a good and close dialogue during the planning phase so that both the municipality and the Armed Forces can prepare good plans

[3425] A defense in and for the entire country

[3426] The Armed Forces have maintained and strengthened their presence in the districts, with particular emphasis in the north

[3427] Well-functioning and attractive local communities are crucial for good basic preparedness, for reducing employee turnover and for supporting the Armed Forces' departments

[3428] The key to this is, among other things, good living and working conditions

[3429] This includes well-functioning housing, service and labor markets, healthcare, transportation and education

[3430] Strengthening these framework conditions requires a broad and cross-sectoral effort

[3431] The government wants to facilitate initiatives in the districts that can contribute to creating good living and working conditions throughout the country

[3432] The defense sector has an ongoing multi-stakeholder salary and incentive project, which has, among other things, looked at measures that can facilitate the settlement of military personnel and their families in the districts

[3433] The project addresses the specifics of the sector and recommends measures within three main areas

[3434] moving, commuting and flexible workplace

[3435] The defense sector can do a lot alone, but increased efforts require cross-sectoral measures

[3436] The Rural Growth Agreements (RGAs) are a concrete example that covers a broad spectrum of measures, where various public sectors and businesses collaborate to achieve common beneficial goals

[3437] By creating good framework conditions, the defense sector will be more successful with incentives that can encourage more people to choose to move and establish themselves in the districts

[3438] Both society and the defense sector have a common interest in creating good and well-functioning local communities that support the Armed Forces' operational capabilities

[3439] Purpose-built and competitive buildings

[3440] The government defines property, buildings and facilities located within military areas as purpose-built buildings

[3441] Purpose-built buildings are often characterized by the difficulty of obtaining alternative premises for the purpose

[3442] Purpose-built buildings are typically designed to serve a specialized purpose, but can also be less specialized buildings in areas without a well-functioning rental market for the type of premises in question

[3443] It was in the St.prop

[3444] No. 84 (1998–99) established five categories that were to be covered by the concept of purpose-built buildings

[3445] Cultural and historical buildings; buildings where special national, cultural or historical considerations indicate that they should be state-owned

[3446] Buildings that have absolutely central functions; buildings that house central functions in state administration, buildings with special security requirements Specially adapted buildings; buildings with a design or location that means few alternative premises

[3447] Properties that lack an active supplier market; buildings that are only offered on long contracts, and that the state will have difficulty getting out of; buildings that provide the landlord with a risk-free investment at the state's expense Other properties; property acquired for state property development, fixed property, property on Svalbard, Bjørnøya and Hopen Competitive buildings are the opposite of purpose-built buildings

[3448] Competitive buildings are characterized by a low degree of customization, and the fact that new premises can easily be found in the existing rental market

[3449] Arrangements for allied training and reception

[3454] The infrastructure is designed for allies, but also provides Norwegian departments with better facilities for education, training and exercises outside of allied activities

[3455] This streamlines strength production

[3456] The government will consider applying the same model elsewhere

[3457] The approach is relevant, among other things, in connection with the Army's core area in inner Troms and at the Air Force's bases

[3459] In Bodø, development is being adapted to the plans for "New city - new airport

[3460] Good shooting and training ranges are also crucial, both on land, in the air and at sea
