[3462] Upgrading and development of infrastructure must take Sami interests into account

[3463] Strengthen measures for climate, nature and the environment on Armed Forces properties

[3464] Escalation in the Armed Forces' activities may have environmental consequences, such as an increase in greenhouse gas emissions and increased pressure on training areas

[3465] The sector's properties, buildings and structures are an important area when the defense sector is to strengthen its efforts to reduce its total climate footprint and negative environmental impact, protect nature and contribute to a sustainable society

[3466] Good environmental management is important to ensure that the Armed Forces can practice and train with the least possible negative consequences for nature and the environment

[3467] Even though the level of activity in the defense sector is to increase, the burden on nature and the environment is to be reduced through environmentally conscious planning and environmental measures

[3468] The sector has long worked well with environmental measures and can draw on a lot of experience

[3469] The defense sector will now step up the implementation of climate and environmental measures on a broad front, and will allocate special funds to facilitate measures that contribute to emission reduction, energy efficiency and biodiversity

[3470] The defense sector is a major user of nature and manages large natural areas

[3471] These areas should be used and managed so that natural diversity is best preserved

[3472] The sector will work to increase natural diversity in fortresses and camps

[3473] The sector shall, through good spatial planning, consideration of natural values during activity and adapted management, facilitate good living environments for endangered and near-endangered species and vulnerable habitats

[3474] This involves setting aside areas for the conservation of natural diversity in the sector's camp plans, establishing flower meadows in camps and fortresses, and otherwise facilitating pollinating insects

[3475] Efforts will also be made to prevent the spread of alien species on defense sector properties

[3476] The Norwegian Armed Forces' environmental officers and expertise groups in the defence agencies will help reduce damage to the environment before and during exercises

[3477] The defense sector is taking mitigating measures for wild reindeer, and will ensure that consideration for wild reindeer is implemented in the instructions for relevant shooting ranges and ranges, as well as having routines for notifying the Norwegian Nature Inspectorate when transporting in such areas

[3478] Pollution shall be kept at the lowest possible level, and the sector shall continue its work on carrying out environmental cleanup and monitoring of pollution

[3479] Examples of measures include reducing chemical leakage at air stations, cleaning up disused shooting and training ranges, and following up with monitoring programs

[3480] Mapping and removal of empty, buried oil tanks will continue

[3481] In the remediation of pollution, runoff and dispersion are also reduced

[3482] Forsvarsbygg has, among other things, removed large amounts of contaminated material in the beach areas at Karljohansvern in Horten – to great benefit to the residents

[3483] It will be built energy-efficiently and with low greenhouse gas emissions, and energy efficiency measures will be implemented that reduce electricity consumption

[3484] This is done, among other things, through energy management to optimize property operations, replacement with LED and sensor-controlled lighting in buildings, electricity saving measures, raising awareness about one's own energy consumption, and by adopting fossil-free solutions where possible

[3485] For example, at Haakonsvern, heat pumps are used that extract heat from the sea and provide both heating and cooling to the buildings as needed

[3486] The defense sector will also work towards a higher degree of self-sufficiency in the sector's bases and camps, thereby increasing local renewable energy production

[3487] The sector has recently established such projects

[3488] For example, solar cells and a battery bank are being installed at Rygge Air Station

[3489] At Ørland Air Station, flexible, mobile and climate-friendly buildings are now being developed for the deployment of F-35 fighter jets

[3490] One of the sub-goals of this project is to reduce the climate footprint of transporting equipment and workshop facilities

[3491] Internal environmental risk analyses are carried out at all shooting and training ranges and facilities

[3492] Camp plans must set aside special consideration zones and land uses to ensure consideration for climate, nature and the environment

[3493] The Norwegian Defence Construction Agency has implemented a system for environmental monitoring plans to be used on new and existing projects

[3494] This sets requirements for environmental management, construction sites and outdoor areas, energy, recycling and waste, substances hazardous to health and the environment, material requirements and emissions to water, soil and air

[3495] See Chapter 10 for a more detailed discussion of the defense sector's work on climate action and climate adaptation

[3496] Cultural and historical properties

[3497] The defense sector is a significant manager of Norwegian cultural heritage and the cultural environment through its responsibility for culturally historic buildings and properties

[3498] A number of listed and protected buildings are in use for military purposes today, and thus constitute a common thread from Norwegian military history to today's defense

[3499] The properties also have significant national value through their connection to significant events in Norway's history, and to the importance of the military for social development and nation-building

[3500] In addition, fortifications and other historic properties are venues for a variety of cultural experiences

[3501] It is the government's goal to preserve the cultural, historical and architectural qualities of the buildings so that this is developed further

[3502] The cultural and historical properties in the defense sector amount to approximately 620,000 square meters, with around 970 buildings that are listed or covered by protection regulations

[3503] There is currently a large maintenance backlog on this property

[3504] The government wants to reduce this through a comprehensive plan to reduce the maintenance backlog for the sector's properties

[3505] The fortresses will be developed as attractive arenas for cultural experiences, tourism and recreation

[3506] The defense sector's fourteen national fortifications and several other border fortifications constitute the majority of the sector's cultural and historical property, with a total of 450 buildings, and represent the largest, thematically coherent part of cultural and historical properties in state ownership

[3507] Military history is conveyed to a large audience, and in 2022 the fortresses had about three million visitors

[3508] The future management of cultural and historical properties is seen in the context of comprehensive management of the sector's property, buildings and facilities, and cooperation with the Armed Forces' museums

[3509] Future-oriented and adaptable defense sector

[3510] The defense sector is dependent on adapting to a rapidly evolving world

[3511] Climate change, technological development and a more complex threat landscape are changing what is needed to defend Norway and who must cooperate to do so

[3512] This places greater demands on the sector's ability to look ahead, be flexible and quickly adapt to new challenges

[3513] The Government will contribute to a more forward-looking and adaptable defense sector by strengthening investment in research and development, placing greater emphasis on innovation, and strengthening work on emission reduction and climate change adaptation

[3514] A common denominator for success in this work is the breakdown of barriers between the military and civilian sectors, so that the actors can come together and benefit from each other

[3515] In addition, greater emphasis must be placed on research and development relevant to the High North

[3516] The rapid development of society means that a successful focus on research, development, innovation and climate adaptation is of great importance for the development of defense capabilities in both the short and long term

[3517] Research and development (R&D) is the sector's most long-term instrument

[3518] The government is facilitating a significant R&D boost and is taking several steps to meet a more complex set of challenges

[3519] The main challenge for today's R&D work is a lack of clearly anchored priorities, too little strategic management, too much emphasis on short-term goals and too little real prioritization

[3520] An increasing number of civilian actors also want to contribute to defense-related R&D, but say that it is challenging to find a way into the defense sector

[3521] On the other hand, the civilian instrument apparatus is not utilized well enough by the defense sector's R&D actors

[3522] In sum, this leads to a lack of coherence between needs and solutions in the civilian and military sectors

[3523] To address this challenge, the government will break down barriers between the military and civilian sectors

[3524] Increased resources are a prerequisite for meeting the challenges and exploiting the opportunities within research and development

[3525] To achieve the greatest possible effect from the initiatives, it is necessary to clearly prioritize what the defense sector's basic knowledge needs are and what is most important for Norway

[3526] Here, R&D is an important tool

[3527] R&D can constitute security policy capital in relation to NATO, the EU, allies and bilateral partners

[3528] R&D can also build bridges between different policy areas

[3529] Therefore, efforts on the civilian and military sides must be seen in context and resources must be better utilized through increased cooperation across sectors

[3530] Similarly, efforts on the national and international sides must be seen in context

[3531] The defense sector's basic knowledge needs The government's priorities within R&D are based on the priorities set for the development of defense capabilities, and the defense sector's basic knowledge needs

[3532] Strategic management of R&D should ensure a balance between the different knowledge needs

[3533] The defense sector's basic knowledge needs concern

[3534] – Groundbreaking knowledge development that explores technological possibilities, new operational capabilities, and new concepts that can realize operational capability

[3535] – Long-term knowledge, technology and capability development related to niche capacities such as missiles, sensor and underwater technology, development of groundbreaking technologies such as artificial intelligence and quantum technology, capability analyses, climate and environmental accounting, knowledge of the High North, research-supported development throughout the life of the equipment, consequences for the application and use of new technology, and innovation potential for new technologies

[3536] – Implementation of adopted policies related to, among other things, prioritized material investments, analyses of triangular cooperation and industrial support, personnel arrangements, and status of implementation

[3537] – Situational understanding for use in decisionmaking, such as technological trends, key developments of importance for security and defense capabilities, security policy analyses, demographic and competence analyses, national capacity in selected research areas, industrial actors' R&D efforts and application of knowledge

[3538] Knowledge-based foundations for developing new policies and setting goals such as research-based advice, analyses, meta-studies, knowledge reviews, thematic knowledge bases and capability gap analyses

[3539] Priorities and initiatives within research and development Norway does not have the resources to be a leader in all defence-related research and development

[3540] Therefore, the government will prioritize niches and build on the comparative advantages Norway already has

[3541] The government's two most important R&D priorities for the defense sector also support how Norway will stand out as an ally and partner

[3542] Norway will lead and participate in multi-domain operations and be at the forefront among allies in situational awareness in the North

[3543] Norway will support the alliance's ability for multi-domain operations

[3544] These are joint operations that exploit the connections between the five areas of warfare: land, sea, air, cyber and space

[3545] Multi-domain operations require the ability to coordinate military and civilian efforts and activities

[3546] Today, there is a gap between the development of individual warfare domains and a multi-domain defense

[3547] Therefore, the government prioritizes R&D activities that integrate and build bridges between the domains, between the civilian and military sectors, develop the ability to understand the situation, and utilize data as a resource for operational purposes

[3548] At the same time, knowledge development that integrates technology, people and organization is also necessary so that the transition to multi-domain operations can occur gradually

[3549] Being at the forefront of situational awareness involves technological innovation and knowledge development that gives the Armed Forces the opportunity for superior and sustained situational awareness and precise decision-making across the entire crisis spectrum

[3550] Situational awareness involves the collection and interpretation of data from all domains across the civilian and military sectors, and includes allied capabilities

[3551] As responsiveness demands increase, faster updates are needed

[3552] This is currently an area with potential for improvement, which the government will give priority to

[3553] The R&D needs are related to developing comprehensive and timely analyses and decision support from combat technical to strategic levels

[3554] This includes space-based information gathering, underwater surveillance technology, and information gathering from sensor systems and unmanned and autonomous systems

[3555] Furthermore, it involves developing how the information will be compiled and presented to relevant personnel at various levels

[3556] The High North is Norway's most important strategic area of interest, and geopolitical tension and climate change are contributing to its increasing importance

[3557] Therefore, the government prioritizes R&D activities that prepare Norway for increased implementation of operations in a cold-weather climate, in the north

[3558] The operating conditions in the high north, especially in winter, require robust solutions that function in demanding climatic conditions

[3559] Cooperation in the operational environment must also be resilient to, among other things, electronic warfare

[3560] This is among the R&D needs that must be prioritized so that Norway can be at the forefront among allies in situational awareness in the North

[3561] Norway will develop future operational capabilities through technological innovation. The government prioritizes R&D activities that develop future operational capabilities through technological innovation

[3562] The armed forces' capacities and systems are expensive, and the government's extensive investment in defence and preparedness will introduce additional capacities

[3563] Therefore, particular emphasis should be placed on R&D that helps to strengthen operational concepts and large weapons platforms

[3564] At the same time, priority should be given to R&D and technological innovation that contributes to increased ability to combat targets at lower cost

[3565] Technological areas such as autonomy and unmanned platforms, combined with groundbreaking technologies such as artificial intelligence, are examples of areas where R&D activities can contribute to giving Norway increased operational effectiveness in both the short and long term

[3566] With this starting point, the government will facilitate four specific R&D initiatives that support the priorities and optimize Norway's defense capability, while at the same time exploiting the opportunities within civil-military and public-private cooperation

[3567] Bridging knowledge development across defense, security and emergency preparedness

[3568] The Government will focus on knowledge development that cuts across defense, security and preparedness, within a national and Nordic framework

[3569] The Government will particularly prioritize knowledge development about complex threats, national vulnerabilities, and see civil resilience in the context of the Armed Forces' operational capability

[3570] The cross-sectoral nature of the topic makes it particularly important to exploit the opportunities inherent in close civil-military cooperation

[3571] A data-driven defense The government will exploit the potential of the large amounts of data produced to further develop the defense sector and develop defense capabilities

[3572] Data must be collected, organized, stored and converted into decision support

[3573] Data lays the foundation for algorithm development in unmanned systems, cyber operations, the exploitation of outer space, and the use of sensor networks

[3574] A secure and future-oriented digital foundation is a prerequisite

[3575] The Armed Forces should exploit the potential of data for operational purposes, but are not data-driven enough today

[3576] At the same time, the military has little experience and expertise when it comes to using artificial intelligence

[3577] A digital transformation is therefore necessary for the Armed Forces to be able to fully participate in multi-domain operations and utilize new or groundbreaking technology

[3578] It is necessary to develop expertise and capacity that can have a lasting effect in the Armed Forces

[3579] The government's commitment to a data-driven defense has a high priority and will be further detailed in collaboration with the Armed Forces and relevant stakeholders

[3580] The government will invest in research and development in groundbreaking technologies such as quantum technology and artificial intelligence to help build national expertise and capacity

[3581] The initiative involves research and development related to the technologies themselves, but also research that sheds light on the consequences and opportunities the technologies provide for Norwegian defense and security

[3582] The initiative will strengthen important expertise and improve the conditions for faster utilization of new technology in the Armed Forces, business and industry

[3583] Realization of the defense sector's strategy for the application of artificial intelligence The defense sector's artificial intelligence strategy has been developed in accordance with the national strategy for artificial intelligence

[3584] The defense sector will exploit the potential of artificial intelligence to help advance Norway's security and defense policy goals

[3585] The ambition is for the defense sector to identify, develop, implement and apply artificial intelligence in a responsible manner

[3586] The most important prerequisite for using artificial intelligence is access to good, standardized and representative data

[3587] The defense sector will therefore begin work on collecting and storing data on a significantly larger scale than today

[3588] Waiting until all the prerequisites are in place is not an option

[3589] A data policy should be established in the defense sector that will define and identify which data is important to collect, and how data can develop military capability and improve task solving

[3590] In order to use and share collected data, a digital infrastructure must be established that enables storage and sharing at all grading levels

[3591] New material must be adapted to support and operate in a structure that facilitates the best possible use of artificial intelligence

[3592] Quantum technology is a multipurpose technology that can potentially provide opportunities for very large computing power, advanced simulation and more accurate sensors

[3593] The government's R&D investment in this area will make Norway better able to exploit the opportunities and handle the challenges that a breakthrough in quantum technology may lead to

[3594] Quantum technology could also have security implications as calculations performed on quantum computers could break current systems for encryption and secure communication

[3595] R&D within quantum-secure crypto algorithms should therefore be strengthened to maintain Norwegian crypto competence

[3596] Artificial intelligence can contribute to increased situational awareness, increased command and control capabilities, the use of space-based sensors for intelligence and surveillance, and the acquisition and utilization of data in all domains

[3597] Artificial intelligence is a multipurpose technology with a variety of applications, and there are professional communities in both the defense sector and the civilian side

[3598] The development of the technology should therefore take place as part of national collaboration

[3599] The government recently launched the "Strategy for Artificial Intelligence for the Defense Sector" where situational awareness, defense against digital threats, and weapons systems are among the focus areas

[3600] The R&D investment in artificial intelligence should be seen in the context of the priorities in this strategy

[3601] Climate change, reuse and recycling

[3602] The Government will invest in research and development related to climate change and climate adaptation

[3603] Melting sea ice in the Arctic, less permafrost, more extreme weather and greater temperature differences will change the Armed Forces' operational areas and thus how operations are carried out

[3604] The Armed Forces will also have to take greater action on climate and environmental measures that can contribute to emission reduction, energy efficiency and biodiversity

[3605] This will place new demands on infrastructure and materials

[3606] Structural changes to increase the effect of research and development In order to get more out of the defense sector's R&D efforts, the government will also implement structural changes to systems and management

[3607] The changes are related to better gathering, coordinating and prioritizing across civilian and military sides, to contribute to better resource utilization across sectors

[3608] More cross-sectoral knowledge and technology collaboration is also necessary to increase society's overall resilience

[3609] The R&D systems on the military and civilian side The government's main approach is to facilitate better coordination between the R&D systems on the military and civilian side

[3610] A common, national research system will be developed that handles Norway's total knowledge needs for both open, protected and classified knowledge

[3611] More people than before will be involved in security and emergency preparedness work, and more businesses will find themselves in situations where security becomes a key consideration

[3612] The Government will facilitate the national research system to be able to handle this

[3613] Therefore, the Research Council, FFI and NSM have been commissioned to deliver a joint proposal for how the future research system should be designed to handle protected, graded research and technology collaboration

[3614] The government will detail this further in the upcoming white paper on the research system

[3615] The government's goal of better coordination of the military and civilian R&D systems also makes it possible to set priorities across public-private and civilian-military divides

[3616] This can help ensure that available resources are utilized more efficiently

[3617] It can also help increase civilian actors' emphasis on R&D aimed at defense, security and emergency preparedness

[3618] Consolidate the defense sector's R&D activities to achieve more strategic and holistic management. There is also a need for better coordination of the defense sector's R&D activities internally within the sector

[3619] Therefore, the government will consolidate the defense sector's R&D activities into a comprehensive and coherent system to increase the ability for strategic and comprehensive management

[3620] To succeed in this, R&D activity must be collected in portfolios and the financing model for research and development must be adapted

[3621] The use of portfolio management means that the government's priorities for developing defense capabilities are translated into specific goals and projects in portfolio plans

[3622] In this way, the management of the defense sector's R&D will change from focusing on each individual project to seeing how a number of projects build up under defined goals in a portfolio

[3623] Strategic management of R&D involves, among other things, prioritizing across portfolios

[3624] To achieve this, it is necessary to view R&D portfolio management in a broader context

[3625] Decisions about resourcing R&D must be informed by other relevant insight and knowledge such as investment plan projects, defense industrial objectives, the lifespan of material systems, and R&D efforts in the civilian sector

[3626] This will make it easier to meet the government's priorities with R&D efforts in the short and long term

[3627] Portfolio management must ensure comprehensive management from research and development, via procurement, to further development in operations

[3628] Increasingly rapid technological development and more complex systems make this more demanding and important

[3741] The defense sector's work on climate action and climate adaptation

[3742] Priorities for climate change adaptation in the defense sector

[3743] The defense sector's activities have a direct impact on the climate and environment through land use, buildings and structures, and emissions from vehicles, aircraft, and vessels

[3744] Therefore, the defense sector must also contribute to national climate and environmental goals

[3745] Climate and nature should be part of all policies and climate and environmental measures should be an integrated part of governance, investment processes, budgets and plans in the sector

[3746] The government's priorities for climate change adaptation follow two tracks

[3747] One emphasizes climate action related to how the defense sector must take its share of responsibility for meeting the government's goals for reduced greenhouse gas emissions

[3748] The second is related to climate adaptation

[3749] In other words, how climate change will affect future threat situations and areas of operation, and place new demands on the development of infrastructure and the Armed Forces' capabilities

[3750] The defense sector must consider how the sector's greenhouse gas emissions can be reduced without compromising the sector's ability to perform its tasks and fulfill its societal goals

[3751] The Armed Forces shall primarily protect Norwegian security

[3752] This means that measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions should not come at the expense of operational defense capabilities

[3753] This is an important and demanding balancing act

[3754] The government's goal is to emphasize climate-friendly solutions without negatively impacting activity levels and operational capabilities

[3755] The defense sector's climate goals should balance an ambition to further reduce the sector's greenhouse gas emissions against the defense's ability to perform its tasks

[3756] This also applies if security policy developments lead to an increased level of operational activity

[3757] A number of initiatives and processes are underway in the work on climate action and climate adaptation in the defense sector

[3758] This applies both to management and implementation, but also in connection with capability development, R&D and innovation

[3759] Important priorities for climate and the environment are already discussed in Chapter 8 on procurement and Chapter 9 on property, buildings and structures

[3760] Emphasis on climate measures in improvement and efficiency work is also discussed in Chapter 11 on governance

[3761] In addition, the government is prioritizing three additional measures

[3762] International knowledge collaboration on climate and security

[3763] As discussed in Chapter 1, climate change is considered a threat multiplier that contributes to intensifying existing conflicts, but also increasingly as an independent security challenge

[3764] This makes good international knowledge collaboration on climate and security important

[3765] Norway contributes financial support and staffing to the NATO Climate Change and Security Center of Excellence in Montreal, Canada

[3766] This is a knowledge center for climate change and security where Norway is one of twelve contributing nations

[3767] The center develops and shares knowledge about the security implications of climate change, how the alliance can adapt to the changing conditions brought about by climate change, and how NATO can work to achieve its goals of reducing the climate footprint of military activities

[3768] Norway staffs one position as section leader at the center, and participates in the center's steering committee

[3769] NATO demands that the alliance become a leader in understanding and countering the consequences of climate change for allied security

[3770] The ambition is being followed up through the NATO Climate Change and Security Action Plan

[3771] The United Kingdom is among the countries that have made visible efforts to reduce their own defense sector's greenhouse gas emissions, including by creating a strategy to make military aviation climate-neutral

[3772] This includes, among other things, a technological focus on fuel reduction measures, testing alternative fuel solutions and carbon capture

[3773] As part of the government's R&D efforts in the defense sector, international knowledge collaboration in this field will also be emphasized

[3774] Emphasis on energy technology that reduces greenhouse gas emissions

[3775] The Norwegian Armed Forces' greenhouse gas emissions are mainly a result of direct emissions from fossil fuels from aircraft and vessels

[3776] Climate change and the green shift will mean that new forms of energy will largely replace traditional fuels in the future

[3777] For the Armed Forces and NATO, security of supply is crucial, while defense-specific equipment is expensive acquisitions with a long lifespan

[3778] This means that the choices made today will bind the defense sector for a long time to come

[3779] Therefore, the government prioritizes that the defense sector plan with energy technology that meets operational needs and requirements for a reduced climate footprint

[3780] The special funds for innovation activities related to climate and environmental measures are part of this priority

[3781] Consistent focus on simulators Training and exercises are crucial for the Armed Forces' operational capability

[3782] Much of the training can be carried out both in the field and using various types of simulators

[3783] The Armed Forces use simulators, among other things, to maximize the utilization of expensive combat platforms

[3784] These help reduce greenhouse gas emissions and the costs associated with the operation and maintenance of systems such as aircraft, vehicles and vessels

[3785] Parts of the exercise can be carried out without causing damage to nature, and without the use of fuel and ammunition

[3786] Simulators can also be used more at times of the year when there is no frost on the ground, or in areas with warmer climates, to reduce the burden on nature

[3787] Climate and environmental impact can be reduced by increased simulator use

[3788] Therefore, the government prioritizes a consistent focus on simulators in the defense sector as a relevant supplement to other training and exercise activities

[3789] Simulators should be prioritized as part of the procurement in all major material projects where the use of a simulator can contribute to increased operational capability and to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and negative environmental impact

[3790] The defense sector's climate and environmental accounts

[3791] The defense sector has a significant climate and environmental footprint

[3792] FFI manages the defense sector's environmental database and annually calculates key environmental aspects and greenhouse gas emissions in the Defense Sector's climate and environmental accounts

[3793] The defense sector's share of Norway's total emissions was 0.5 percent in

[3794] Greenhouse gas emissions are divided into indirect and direct emissions

[3795] Indirect emissions include, among other things, subcontractors' emissions in the production and transport of goods, services, and travel activities

[3796] The largest direct emissions are fossil fuels from the Navy's vessels and the Air Force's aircraft, with 48 percent and 37 percent respectively, followed by emissions from vehicles, buildings and construction

[3797] The Armed Forces' direct emissions are closely related to the Armed Forces' level of activity, and with increased activity, emissions will increase

[3798] For example, the Armed Forces' direct greenhouse gas emissions increased by two percent from

[3799] This is mainly related to increased activity levels, including as a consequence of security policy developments and the war in Ukraine

[3800] The direct emissions from the defense sector are part of the nonemission sector and thus not part of the EU's emissions trading system, but the sector currently pays a CO2 tax for greenhouse gas emissions from the use of fossil fuels

[3801] The defense sector's climate and environmental strategy

[3802] The agencies in the sector have developed a joint climate and environmental strategy with an associated action plan

[3803] These documents contain overall goals that will help the defense sector reduce its total climate footprint and safeguard nature and environmental concerns

[3804] The documents also aim to help ensure that the defense sector is prepared for and adapted to climate change and its consequences

[3805] The most important goals in the strategy are related to greenhouse gas reduction measures in the Navy, and reducing the defense sector's emissions by 20 percent by 2030, compared to the level

[3806] Other measures include phasing in zero-emission technology for administrative vehicles by 2025, zero-emission solutions for construction sites, and reducing purchased energy by 10 percent

[3807] Better governance of the defense sector

[3808] The extensive investment in increased defense capabilities that the government is planning will require a significant share of society's total resources

[3809] This leads to increased expectations that the Armed Forces and the defense sector manage resources in a responsible manner, in line with the Storting's decision

[3810] The defense sector is organized as a continuous value chain with four agencies, where the bulk of results and effects are realized in the form of military capability in the Armed Forces

[3811] The main arguments for this organization are that it facilitates specialization and competence effects within various management areas, while at the same time ensuring that responsibility for the final result and effects can be clearly assigned

[3812] This is illustrated by the fact that Defence Materiel is Norway's largest public procurer, while Defence Buildings manages Norway's largest public property portfolio

[3813] Over time, a number of challenges related to strategic management and goal achievement have been identified in the implementation of the defense sector's long-term plans

[3814] One of the challenges with the organization has been establishing effective interfaces and effective interaction between agencies across the value chain

[3815] This challenge is to some extent exacerbated by unclear interfaces between the Armed Forces and the Ministry of Defense, as a result of the practice of the integrated strategic management model

[3816] For example, the ministry has had an operational role in planning and managing areas that in other state administrations normally lie at directorate and agency level

[3817] Over time, this has created ambiguity in roles and responsibilities between agencies and ministries, and between agencies in the defense sector

[3818] The security policy situation reinforces the need to make changes in the management of the defense sector, so that defense capabilities can be strengthened through a rapid escalation

[3819] The work on changes in governance has been ongoing in parallel with the work on a new long-term plan, and the goal is for the bulk of the changes to be implemented during 2024, in parallel with the implementation of this long-term plan being planned and prepared in the ministry and agencies

[3820] The government has based this long-term plan on the fact that the organization of the defense sector will essentially remain as it is today

[3821] Better governance of the sector will be achieved through various measures for better collaboration, and a review of roles and responsibilities

[3822] Organization of the defense sector

[3823] The Ministry of Defence is responsible for formulating and implementing security and defence policy

[3824] This entails responsibility for implementing adopted defense policy ambitions that the Storting has adopted or endorsed

[3825] The defense sector consists of agencies with different roles and responsibilities, where most of the resources in the sector contribute to achieving goals that are taken up by the Defense

[3826] The Ministry of Defence is responsible for the agency management of the Armed Forces, Defence Materiel, Defence Buildings and the Defence Research Institute

[3827] The management of the Armed Forces is based on specific performance targets, and the other agencies in the sector shall support and contribute to the Armed Forces' performance targets

[3828] The Chief of Defence is the head of the Norwegian Armed Forces, and is supported by the Defence Staff

[3829] This means that the Chief of Defence is responsible for the overall management, planning and daily operation of the Armed Forces' activities, within the political priorities that form the basis of this long-term plan

[3830] With this comes responsibility for achieved results and for the Armed Forces' finances

[3831] Defence Materiel is responsible for acquiring, delivering and disposing of materiel for the Armed Forces in line with adopted plans, in a cost-effective, sustainable and safe manner

[3832] Defence Construction is responsible for acquiring and managing cost-effective and functional property, buildings and structures (EBA) in the defence sector

[3833] The Norwegian Defence Research Institute shall provide the political and military leadership with research-based and independent advice on the development of the defence sector

[3834] The National Security Authority (NSM) is a cross-sectoral directorate with professional and supervisory authority for preventive security

[3835] The Ministry of Justice and Public Security is responsible for agency management of NSM

[3836] The Ministry of Defence has instructional authority over NSM in matters within the Ministry's area of responsibility, and the directorate is therefore also technically subordinate to the Ministry in certain areas

[3837] Box 11.1 The development of a robust security service

[3838] A new security policy situation means that attention to internal security in the defense sector must be strengthened

[3839] The adversary's use of complex threats and instruments could both directly and indirectly affect the Armed Forces and the defense sector, with the intention of undermining our operational capabilities in peace and crisis

[3840] The Government considers that a systematic and comprehensive commitment to a robust security service will be important for maintaining and protecting the capabilities and functions of the Armed Forces in the face of complex threats, and with vulnerable value chains across and outside the sector

[3841] Security work in the Armed Forces and the defense sector is about the ability to fulfill the Security Act's requirements to prevent, detect and counteract security-threatening activities in all domains

[3842] Security work is divided into preventive security, in the sense of protecting the defense sector's fundamental national functions (GNF) and national security interests (NSI), as well as the Armed Forces' own ability to detect and counter security-threatening activities

[3843] Cross-sectoral value chains and dependencies mean that vulnerabilities in civilian sectors can affect the Armed Forces' operational capability, both directly and indirectly

[3844] This places demands on the Armed Forces' overall security understanding and ability to adequately control the Armed Forces' dependencies

[3845] The defense sector must to a greater extent be a premise provider for security work in the civilian sectors that support the Defense and national security

[3846] The Government intends to strengthen the security service in the Armed Forces to have sufficient capacity to prevent, counteract and handle security-threatening activities in and against the defense sector in a new security policy situation

[3847] The government is planning a systematic and comprehensive initiative that will give the sector sufficient ability to implement measures and procedures, based on comprehensive risk management from a strategic level

[3848] Establishment of the Defence History Museum The Defence Museums shall manage, research and disseminate Norway's defence, military, war and post-war history and the military cultural heritage and tradition

[3849] The activity will manage the state's ownership of military material and national cultural heritage worthy of preservation in order to safeguard and convey historical knowledge to future generations

[3850] The government has decided to modernize museum operations by lifting the museum operations out of the Armed Forces and establishing the operations as an agency under the Ministry of Defense

[3851] It is planned to establish the agency

[3852] The Museum of Defence History will include the museums that currently constitute the Armed Forces Museums

[3853] The government's goal is for the Museum of Defence History to be attractive and relevant to the entire population, and for the museum to contribute to building a will to defend and highlighting the efforts of Norwegian veterans

[3854] Measures for better governance of the defense sector

[3855] The government's measures for better governance of the defense sector are being implemented as part of the government's confidence reform (box

[3856] The goal of the management changes is to achieve the highest possible defense capability and to get more out of the funds allocated to the sector

[3857] The fundamental starting point for the changes is the clarification of roles, responsibilities and authority between agencies and ministries, and between agencies

[3858] This will make it more possible to place clear and comprehensive responsibility for goals and results with the individual agency head

[3859] The starting point for management will be clear and agreed performance targets across the defense sector, based on the objectives in this long-term plan

[3860] It may be necessary to make adjustments in the implementation

[3861] The Government intends for the annual budget processes to be used in a more active manner in handling challenges and when adjustments are needed in the implementation of the long-term plan

[3862] The Government will systematically update the status of the implementation of the plan, including goal achievement and reasons for any deviations, new assessment of risks in the implementation, and any need for changes

[3863] It is necessary to improve collaboration in the sector

[3864] The defense sector handles complex issues that require interdisciplinary problem-solving

[3865] This requires good working methods, a culture of collaboration and trust between agencies

[3866] A prerequisite is that the leaders of the agencies in the defense sector align their activities towards common goals, and that the leaders are held accountable for the sub-goals they can influence

[3867] The government's confidence reform in the defense sector

[3868] The confidence reform in the defense sector aims to facilitate a sector with higher implementation capacity and faster adaptations to changing conditions

[3869] It will contribute to increased defense capability and efficiency, in order to be better able to meet the challenges and achieve political objectives

[3870] The changes are intended to help ensure that the management of the defense sector is more in line with other central government departments

[3871] This involves clear dividing lines between ministries and underlying agencies, and overall responsibility for goals and results in the agencies

[3872] In 2022, the government initiated a comprehensive, sequential review of various areas in the defense sector, to review and assess how the sector works with important processes

[3873] This includes, among other things, a review of the areas of procurement, maintenance, ICT, building and property management, investments, personnel and expertise, research and development (R&D), and operations

[3874] The review also included the Ministry of Defence's management processes

[3875] In the work of reviewing the various areas, emphasis has been placed on close dialogue with employee organizations

[3876] The review of all areas should be completed within

[3877] Measures for better management of the various areas will be implemented continuously

[3878] The Armed Forces shall have a leadership role in planning and implementation. The division of tasks between the Ministry of Defence and the agencies in the sector has partly been an obstacle to comprehensive and effective management

[3879] The Ministry of Defence must therefore, to a greater extent, concentrate on tasks related to policy development and the role as a secretariat for political leadership

[3880] The government wants the Chief of Defence to have greater functions in his own organisation that are important for the development and management of the Armed Forces

[3881] This concerns functions related to planning and development of areas such as personnel and investments

[3882] The Chief of Defence is given coordinating authority across the sector

[3883] The Armed Forces shall have a leading role in contributing to the comprehensive development of the defense sector, in close cooperation with other agencies

[3884] The Armed Forces' enhanced role in planning and implementation will lead to better coordination in the development of various input factors such as property, buildings and structures, personnel, materiel and ICT

[3885] The Government wants the Armed Forces to develop the ability to plan, develop and manage its own activities in the short and long term

[3886] This means that the Defence Staff must have processes, expertise, capacity, continuity, organisation and culture to plan and manage the Defence's activities holistically

[3887] The Armed Forces' resources should be prioritized based on what provides the greatest overall goal achievement, within given political frameworks

[3888] The Armed Forces must have a sufficient overall overview of the prerequisites, status and challenges in structural development

[3889] Based on this, the Armed Forces will identify needs for reprioritization, which will be communicated to the Ministry

[3890] This also entails a need for changes in how the management model in the defence sector should operate and be practiced, see discussion in box 11.3. The defence sector should be given increased freedom of action within the area of personnel and expertise

[3891] This will create the conditions for the Chief of Defence to be able to plan the implementation of political decisions within political priorities, and manage and staff the Armed Forces with enough personnel with the right expertise

[3892] The Armed Forces shall have overall responsibility for managing all military personnel in the defense sector

[3893] To meet this increased responsibility, the Armed Forces must strengthen its capacity and expertise in the field

[3894] Investment activities are closely linked to the Armed Forces' structural and capability development

[3895] Parts of the responsibility related to investments that currently lie with the Ministry of Defence will be transferred to the Armed Forces

[3896] The Armed Forces, with support from Defence Materiel and Defence Construction, will be given more comprehensive responsibility for planning and managing the investment portfolio to achieve the objectives in this long-term plan

[3897] ICT is a crucial factor for implementation capability and goal achievement in most areas of the defense sector

[3898] In the area of ICT, the defense sector has had challenges related to insufficient implementation capacity, unclear roles and responsibilities, and weak governance

[3899] The Government therefore wants the Armed Forces' management of ICT, including management of the Armed Forces' secure platforms, to be consolidated into one function within the Armed Forces

[3900] The goal is that this provides a better basis for choosing the right ICT solutions for the Armed Forces, and for implementing them more quickly

[3901] Integrated Strategic Management (ISL Model) The management model in the defense sector is called Integrated Strategic Management (ISL) and was established

[3902] The ISL model contributes to closeness between the political and military strategic levels, and means that the Ministry of Defense has both civilian and military employees

[3903] The ministry is also co-located with the Defence Staff, which contributes to good coordination of management in the defence sector

[3904] The Chief of Defence is the head of the Norwegian Armed Forces, and is also a professional military advisor to the ministry

[3905] The advisory function means that the Chief of Defence will contribute to work on overall strategic themes and issues related to situational awareness, the use of military power, crisis management, and in the work on the overall development of the defence sector

[3906] The Chief of Defence shall provide professional military advice related to the specific development of the defence structure

[3907] To strengthen the Chief of Defence's ability for strategic management and at the same time clarify roles and responsibilities, professional military advice and studies related to the specific development of the defence structure should originate from the Armed Forces and the Defence Staff

[3908] Since 2003, it has been a prerequisite for the ISL model that the Defence Staff should be an implementation staff of limited scope

[3909] This has meant that the Defence Staff currently does not have sufficient ability to manage and develop the overall activities of the Defence Forces

[3910] There is therefore a need to change the practice of the ISL model to strengthen the Chief of Defence's ability for strategic management

[3911] The Defence Staff will in future be further developed with increased ability to manage and develop the Armed Forces' activities in a holistic manner, within the framework decided by political leadership, in order to achieve the objectives in the long-term plan for the defence sector

[3912] More efficient procurements combined in Defence Equipment and Defence Buildings

[3913] There are currently partly overlapping procurement environments in the agencies of the Armed Forces, Defence Materiel and Defence Construction

[3914] The review of the procurement area has identified potential for both streamlining and professionalizing procurement functions in the sector

[3915] The government will consolidate the defense sector's procurement functions into the agencies Defence Materiel and Defence Construction, with a common procurement strategy

[3916] It is assumed that a common procurement environment will be established in Defence Materiel, which includes both the existing environment for investment procurement in Defence Materiel, and the current environment for operational procurement in the Armed Forces

[3917] Work on further detailed planning and implementation is ongoing

[3918] The goal is to shorten the time from need to delivery, as well as achieve better agreements through increased quality and lower procurement costs

[3919] The Armed Forces shall have overall responsibility for the maintenance of materiel

[3920] The review of the Armed Forces' maintenance has shown that the availability of the Armed Forces' equipment in daily force production and operations is too low, and that maintenance costs are high

[3921] Maintenance processes take too long, partly because responsibility and authority are distributed among many actors

[3922] The Government will give the Armed Forces a clearer overall responsibility for the maintenance of equipment during the operational phase

[3923] This means that the Armed Forces must be able to influence all priorities that have a bearing on materiel availability, even where operation and maintenance tasks are carried out by other agencies in the sector

[3924] The goal is to achieve increased operational capability through increased availability and uptime of the equipment

[3925] It is also a goal to achieve lower unit costs through more efficient processes and a clear division of tasks between Defence Materiel and the Armed Forces

[3926] Improvement and efficiency in the sector An evaluation of the efficiency work in the period 2021–2024 has identified four main challenges in the work on improvement and efficiency

[3927] Firstly, there is perceived to be insufficient correspondence between the Defence Forces' overall goals and the goals of the improvement and efficiency work

[3928] It is perceived as a savings and cuts program that does not provide incentives for improvements related to the Armed Forces' overall goals

[3929] There has been a one-sided focus on lasting reductions in operating costs, which means that several gains are not qualified and reported

[3930] Secondly, lack of access to data and analysis capacity creates challenges with documentation and visibility of results

[3931] Thirdly, it has proven to be challenging to conduct improvement and efficiency work across agencies

[3932] Fourth, there is great variation in organizational maturity in implementing change projects and continuous improvement

[3933] In this long-term plan, the government will strengthen the requirements for improvement and efficiency work

[3934] To succeed and contribute to the highest possible defense capability within given resource limits, the organization of the work must change

[3935] Three principles are used to strengthen the work on improvement and efficiency in the defense sector

[3936] The first is that the goals for efficiency improvement must be linked more directly to defense capability

[3937] This means that the work is integrated into business management and development and is more closely linked to the achievement of strategic goals and the Storting's adopted ambition

[3938] The second is a broader definition of benefits in line with the recommendations of the Directorate for Financial Management, and that benefits are planned and managed based on quality, financial and societal benefits

[3939] The third is that the allocation of profits must contribute to the highest possible goal achievement and reduce risk

[3940] Improvement and efficiency work must be integrated as part of business development and management at all agencies in the sector

[3941] This means that new measures are identified, implemented and documented as part of the agencies' ordinary planning and implementation processes

[3942] It is important that responsibility for implementing measures is clearly placed within the agencies

[3943] It will also be important to make the work more data-driven and to improve the quality of available data

[3944] Furthermore, the sector's profit accounting and ability to create good profit plans with quantifiable measurement indicators and zeropoint measurements will be further developed

[3945] Productivity measurements for operations and main processes will give the sector the opportunity to measure overall performance improvements

[3946] By increasing the precision and quality of the databases, the sector will gain a better overview of the effects of the improvement measures and greater opportunities for learning and management

[3947] The government places emphasis on following up on the expected realization of benefits from the previous long-term plan, and expects to have realized remaining efficiency gains by the end of

[3948] In addition, this long-term plan aims to realize gains of at least NOK 2.5 billion by

[3949] The goal is that at least one third of the amount can be reallocated in the annual budgets

[3950] The remaining gains must be documented based on approved procedures and calculation models and made visible in the state budget and in relevant reporting

[3951] The allocation of released funds shall be assessed in each budget year against objectives and initiatives and shall not be included in the long-term plan's planning framework

[3952] Further release of economic gains through improvement and efficiency can be used to accelerate the strengthening of defense capabilities, reduce challenges and risks in the implementation of the long-term plan, contribute to financing the escalation of this defense pledge, or be reprioritized to other parts of the state administration

[3953] The defense promise over time

[3954] This long-term plan has been developed in a time of seriousness

[3955] Several developments and trends could influence the framework factors and premises for implementing the plan

[3956] Long-term developments and trends As described in Chapter 1, Norway faces a demanding security policy situation in the years to come

[3957] Developments will depend, among other things, on how Russia rebuilds its military capabilities over time and positions itself in our region, also as a response to Sweden and Finland's membership in NATO

[3958] Russia's development will affect our own choices and priorities, as well as those of our allies and NATO

[3959] Norway and our allies are facing major changes, and it is challenging to predict when these will take full effect

[3960] Technological development has been ongoing for several decades

[3961] Ahead of us lies the potential of artificial intelligence, unmanned and autonomous systems, and space-based technology that will impact societies, international power relations, interdependencies, value chains, and production systems

[3962] It is expected that this will change the way military power is used

[3963] Climate change is among the biggest challenges the world faces

[3964] These will affect the security policy challenge picture and could contribute to conflict patterns that we cannot currently foresee

[3965] At the same time, new requirements for reduced emissions could radically change key premises for the defense sector's organization and operations

[3966] The green shift will affect our macroeconomics

[3967] These are trends that affect most countries in the Western community of values

[3968] Norway is well equipped to meet these challenges, while the room for maneuver in the Norwegian economy will also necessitate stricter priorities going forward

[3969] The focus on defense and preparedness that is necessary to implement the defense pledge will require sobriety in other areas, but is necessary to safeguard our national interests and our democratic society

[3970] Our society will also increasingly be characterized by demographic changes, competition for labor between sectors, and career aspirations that create a more dynamic working life, with more frequent changes in career plans, workplaces, and employers

[3971] This is an issue that affects more sectors than just the defense sector

[3972] The Armed Forces' increased personnel needs require new measures to recruit and retain employees, and are a prerequisite for success with the defense pledge

[3973] As described in the defense concept, Norway's defense capability also depends on the will to defend among the population, the resilience of society, and civil-military cooperation within the framework of total defense

[3974] Technological and demographic developments also influence each other and will shape the design, organization and application of military power in the years ahead

[3975] Principles for continuous and long-term defense planning

[3976] A holistic approach

[3977] The challenges facing the defense sector are unpredictable and complex, with many and increasing interdependencies, both in terms of the nature of the challenges and the means to meet them effectively

[3978] This requires a holistic approach to the further development of the defense sector

[3979] Key decisions and choices in individual areas must always be made with an eye towards the whole – across the sector, compared to other sectors, and in an international perspective

[3980] This places great and increasing demands on defense planning

[3981] At the same time, it will never be possible to establish a comprehensive picture of all connections and consequences before decisions are made

[3982] A fundamental principle in defense planning is to strive for the greatest possible degree of comprehensiveness in planning

[3983] Predictable framework and long-term balance

[3984] The government's defense planning must have a long-term perspective in which short, medium and long-term measures are seen in context and coordinated with each other

[3985] This is reinforced by the fact that the defense sector is an investment- and expertise-intensive business

[3986] This is not unique to the defense sector

[3987] The long lead times traditionally associated with the development and procurement of complex military equipment and the in-house production of specialized professional expertise in a number of areas mean that decisions made today will only have an effect many years into the future, thereby placing significant constraints on the future

[3988] This requires that defense planning must be based on a sufficient degree of predictability regarding the long-term framework for the sector's activities, both in terms of finances and overall level of ambition

[3989] At the same time, the rapid change and complexity in our environment, which is described in this proposition, entails a need to be able to more quickly extract effects from the funds allocated to the sector, and a need to be able to adjust the course along the way when this is required

[3990] The measures that this proposition recommends within procurement, in the area of personnel and expertise, and related to changes in management, contribute to underpinning this

[3991] Flexibility and freedom of action that underpin long-term balance

[3992] In the future, defense planning will be designed to establish sufficient flexibility and freedom of action to be able to rebalance and reprioritize along the way in order to achieve politically determined objectives

[3993] The sector must strengthen its ability for continuous change

[3994] This includes the ability and willingness to differentiate the details of the decisions that are made

[3995] Concrete decisions and resolutions should be prioritized where there is the greatest certainty regarding the effect in the short and medium term, and where the measures are also robust in a long-term perspective and can be supported by sufficient implementation capacity

[3996] In other areas, it would be more appropriate to establish a more overall approach to the development of the sector, with more flexibility that enables continuous development, including reprioritization and changes

[3997] This will create a more robust starting point for meeting rapid changes in a complex challenge landscape

[3998] It will also facilitate the realization of the politically determined objectives for the sector's further development in the most efficient way possible, ensuring the long-term balance between the sector's tasks, ambitions and resources

[3999] Realism, efficient resource utilization and power in implementation

[4000] Defense planning must be based on the greatest possible degree of realism

[4001] This is related both to the assumptions on which the plans are based, and to the sector's ability to realize the plans

[4002] Looking back in time, there are a number of examples where the plans have proven to be too optimistic, that too much risk has been taken in the overall level of ambition, or that the sector has not been able to implement the plans in accordance with the assumptions that have been made

[4003] This may be due to both internal sectoral conditions and external developments and factors that the sector itself has little control over

[4004] Realistic planning must seek to take into account that both are very likely to occur over time, and to structure the plans in such a way that this can be handled with the least possible consequence for the overall achievement of the goals

[4005] The Community provides significant resources for the defence sector

[4006] This also means that high demands must be made on resources being managed efficiently and in such a way that the greatest possible defense capability is created from every krone

[4007] This is also crucial for the will to defend and society's trust in the sector

[4008] The significant defense boost

[4009] The government's recommendations in this plan will place great demands on the sector's ability to implement and manage the business

[4010] The Government has therefore recommended several measures in this proposal to facilitate better governance and implementation

[4011] The measures will constitute important prerequisites for a good and vigorous implementation of the long-term plan for the defense sector with the aim of making the most efficient use of allocated resources

[4012] The measures are intended to improve the sector's implementation capacity, increase efficiency and lay the foundation for faster adaptation to changes

[4013] Joint ownership and necessary expertise Realizing the level of ambition that the government recommends for the further development of the defense sector in this proposition requires joint ownership and commitment to the overall goal and the fundamental assumptions and framework on which this is based

[4014] This must persist over time and across political divides

[4015] The implementation of the long-term defense plans spans several governments and parliamentary terms

[4016] A crucial prerequisite for successful implementation of the plans will therefore be that they are followed up over time with a level of funding that follows up on the financial planning assumptions on which they are based

[4017] It will also be crucial that different parts of the sector themselves are able to pull together to realize the political goals and ambitions that are adopted

[4018] The starting point must be shared ownership of the assumptions that form the basis for the plan and the changes that will occur along the way

[4019] A fragmented approach to this work will create significant challenges both in implementation and in ongoing defense planning

[4020] The Defence Pledge for Norway's Security

[4021] The defense pledge recommended by the government in this proposal will provide a solid foundation for further developing a robust national defense and a significantly strengthened contribution to allied security

[4022] At the same time, a rapid and significant strengthening of the Armed Forces places great demands on the sector's implementation capacity

[4023] The realization of the defense promise will require the sector to be able to think in new ways when translating goals and ambitions into increased defense capability

[4024] This includes the ability and willingness to adopt new approaches and instruments, but also to be able to adjust and improve traditional processes and ways of thinking and remove formal and informal obstacles to effective implementation

[4025] The implementation of substantial increases in funding to support a rapid strengthening of the Armed Forces, which is based on interdependence between many different measures over time, also entails significant risks

[4026] Great attention must therefore be paid to ongoing risk management, where mitigating measures can be implemented early if necessary and where transparency about developments in the challenge picture is necessary as a basis for making new political decisions about necessary course changes along the way

[4027] This will also require a good and open dialogue between the government and the Storting, not only when this plan is presented, but also in future parliamentary terms

[4028] The government is now laying the foundation for a safer Norway through an ambitious defense boost

[4029] Defense capabilities are built over time

[4030] In implementing the plan, we will make choices that maintain financial sustainability and balance between tasks, ambitions and resources over time

[4031] The ambitions and choices in this plan have implications for defense capabilities

[4032] also beyond

[4033] The most fundamental prerequisite for success in the continuous work of further developing the defense sector in the face of new and complex challenges will be that the sector is able to recruit, further develop and retain the necessary expertise in the organization

[4034] This work will require both new and continuously updated insight, but also the necessary continuity to succeed

[4035] Ultimately, it is the people who will prepare, implement and keep the defense promise

[4046] The Chief of Defence's comments on the long-term plan

[4047] The government has presented an ambitious long-term plan for the defense sector that proposes a comprehensive strengthening of the Armed Forces

[4048] A more serious security situation means that increased investment in the Armed Forces is a correct and important priority

[4049] The long-term plan is in line with the Chief of Defence's expert military advice "Security in uncertain times", as well as other advice and input

[4050] It describes a challenging picture and a necessary strengthening of defense capabilities on which there is broad agreement

[4051] The plan emphasizes a balance between tasks, ambitions, structure and resources, both in the short and long term

[4052] This ambitious long-term plan places a great responsibility for implementation on the entire defense sector

[4053] It is a responsibility that the Armed Forces and the sector take on with great seriousness, and with the certainty that it is right to spend more of the community's resources on security in the years to come

[4054] The long-term plan is a major joint boost for the defense sector, which requires good control, collaboration and great implementation ability

[4055] Since the transfer of the professional military council, it has become even more important to strengthen the Armed Forces

[4056] Russia's rearmament is proceeding faster than previously expected

[4057] Increasing great power rivalry means that European countries must take greater responsibility within the framework of NATO, and although Swedish and Finnish membership strengthens the alliance, it also entails increased responsibility for Norway as a receiving and transit country for military reinforcements for the entire Arctic

[4058] Strengthening the Armed Forces

[4059] The long-term plan takes comprehensive steps to increase the Armed Forces' combat capability, and strengthens the input factors on which the Armed Forces depend in a good and responsible manner

[4060] The focus on personnel and expertise, infrastructure, spare parts and ammunition is fundamental to strengthening the current structure and facilitating better utilization of the Armed Forces' capacities

[4061] The ability for increased presence, surveillance, and command and control will contribute to increased situational awareness

[4062] The government's investment in space and long-range drones is central here

[4063] Together with the 2024 Fleet Plan, this is an important contribution to strengthening control over Norway's large sea areas and Norwegian territory

[4064] The modernization of the surface structure in the Navy is very important for our defense capability

[4065] The new fleet plan provides long-term perspective and predictability in the development of the Navy

[4066] Standardization will provide increased availability and more efficient maintenance of new vessels

[4067] Long-termism and predictability can also contribute to building competence and establishing greater capacity in Norwegian industry, thereby strengthening national defense capabilities and preparedness

[4068] The focus on air defense is absolutely necessary, as the war in Ukraine has shown

[4069] Technology development is moving rapidly

[4070] NASAMS has proven effective and it is therefore right to first invest more in what we already have

[4071] Air defense must also be strengthened in several layers, from anti-drone capacity to long-range air defense

[4072] Strengthening the Army, the Home Guard and the Special Forces gives the Armed Forces increased capacity for our national defense

[4073] In addition, the Armed Forces will have a better ability to contribute to NATO's collective defense, in the Nordic region or in other parts of NATO's area of ​​responsibility

[4074] The government's focus on personnel in the Armed Forces is a fundamental prerequisite for further growth, and the long-term plan introduces a number of positive personnel and competence measures

[4075] The measures provide greater scope for action to develop and strengthen the personnel and expertise area in the future

[4076] In the coming years, it will be essential to be able to meet changes in the security situation and take advantage of continuous technological developments

[4077] The Norwegian Armed Forces have experience in quickly translating new technology and knowledge into operational use, through an innovative approach in close collaboration between defense, research and industry

[4078] This requires necessary interaction between the defense sector, research communities and the business community

[4079] It is therefore good that the government has found room for a significant investment in innovation, climate adaptation, and research and development

[4080] A great responsibility rests on the Armed Forces and the defense sector to achieve rapid impact from the resources prioritized for increased defense capability

[4081] Many countries will strengthen their defenses in the future

[4082] Therefore, production capacity and delivery ability are under great pressure and prices are increasing

[4083] For this long-term plan to have the effect that the Storting, the government and the Norwegian people expect, it is crucial to have better cooperation in the defense sector as well as modernization and streamlining of maintenance and procurement processes

[4084] The sector reform being implemented in the defense sector will contribute to better cooperation, interaction and clearer responsibilities

[4085] Faster, more efficient and more flexible implementation does not happen by itself

[4086] Therefore, the plan must have sufficient flexibility and room for maneuver

[4087] As Chief of Defence, it is my task to implement the political recommendations in this long-term plan in a way that makes the best possible use of the resources the Armed Forces have been given

[4088] The government's long-term plan for the defense sector is a clear response to a more serious security situation

[4089] The government is presenting an ambitious and absolutely necessary initiative

[4090] It will make Norway far better equipped to meet the security situation and takes powerful steps to create a solid Norwegian defense capability within the framework of NATO
